# Page: Overview

# Overview

## Purpose and Scope

TorchANI-Amber is a high-performance interface that integrates neural network potentials from the ANI family with the Amber molecular dynamics simulation suite. This system enables both full machine learning (ML) simulations where the entire potential energy surface is computed by neural networks, and hybrid ML/MM simulations where quantum mechanical regions are handled by neural networks while molecular mechanical regions use classical force fields.

This document provides a technical overview of the system architecture, core components, and integration mechanisms. For detailed installation instructions, see [Installation and Build](#2.1). For simulation configuration details, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For performance testing information, see [Benchmarking System](#5).

## System Architecture

The following diagram illustrates the overall system architecture, showing how the various components interact during runtime:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Build System"
        CMAKE["CMakeLists.txt<br/>Build Configuration"]
        JIT_PY["jit/jit.py<br/>Model Compilation"]
        MODELS["Pre-trained Models<br/>ANI1x, ANI2x, AimNet2"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Runtime Engine"
        TORCHANI_CPP["torchani.cpp<br/>C++ Implementation"]
        TORCHANI_H["torchani.h<br/>C API Interface"]
        GLOBAL_CONFIG["GlobalConfig<br/>Device & Precision"]
        JIT_MODELS["JIT Models<br/>.pt files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Amber Integration Layer"
        TORCHANI_F90["torchani.F90<br/>Fortran Interface"]
        EXTPOT["External Potential<br/>iextpot=1"]
        QMMM["QM/MM Interface<br/>ifqnt=1"]
        MDIN["mdin Configuration<br/>&ani namelist"]
    end
    
    subgraph "MD Engines"
        SANDER["sander<br/>Amber MD Engine"]
        PMEMD["pmemd<br/>Amber MD Engine"]
    end
    
    CMAKE --> JIT_PY
    JIT_PY --> JIT_MODELS
    MODELS --> JIT_MODELS
    
    JIT_MODELS --> TORCHANI_CPP
    TORCHANI_CPP --> TORCHANI_H
    GLOBAL_CONFIG --> TORCHANI_CPP
    
    TORCHANI_H --> TORCHANI_F90
    MDIN --> EXTPOT
    MDIN --> QMMM
    
    TORCHANI_F90 --> SANDER
    EXTPOT --> SANDER
    QMMM --> SANDER
    EXTPOT --> PMEMD
    TORCHANI_F90 --> PMEMD
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:1-918](), [include/torchani.h](), [jit/jit.py:1-180](), [README.md:9-18]()

## Core Runtime Components

### C++ Computational Engine

The core computational engine is implemented in `torchani.cpp` and provides the primary interface between Amber and PyTorch. Key global components include:

| Component | Type | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| `model` | `torch::jit::Module` | Loaded JIT-compiled neural network model |
| `torchani_atomic_numbers` | `torch::Tensor` | Atomic numbers tensor for the system |
| `config` | `GlobalConfig` | Device, precision, and runtime configuration |
| `torchani_builtin_models` | `std::vector<std::string>` | List of supported model names |

The following diagram shows the data flow through the C++ engine:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        COORDS["coords_buf[][]<br/>Atomic Coordinates"]
        ATOMIC_NUMS["atomic_nums[]<br/>Element Types"]
        CELL["cell_buf[][]<br/>Unit Cell"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tensor Building"
        DBL_BUF_TO_COORDS["dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()"]
        DBL_BUF_TO_CELL["dbl_buf_to_cell_tensor()"]
        SETUP_INPUTS["setup_inputs_pbc()<br/>setup_inputs_nopbc()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Execution"
        MODEL_FORWARD["model.forward()"]
        JIT_IVALUE["torch::jit::IValue<br/>Output Tuple"]
        VALIDATE["validate_model_output()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Processing"
        CALC_FORCES["calculate_and_populate_forces()"]
        POP_ENERGY["populate_potential_energy()"]
        POP_CHARGES["populate_atomic_charges()"]
    end
    
    COORDS --> DBL_BUF_TO_COORDS
    ATOMIC_NUMS --> SETUP_INPUTS
    CELL --> DBL_BUF_TO_CELL
    
    DBL_BUF_TO_COORDS --> SETUP_INPUTS
    DBL_BUF_TO_CELL --> SETUP_INPUTS
    SETUP_INPUTS --> MODEL_FORWARD
    
    MODEL_FORWARD --> JIT_IVALUE
    JIT_IVALUE --> VALIDATE
    VALIDATE --> CALC_FORCES
    VALIDATE --> POP_ENERGY
    VALIDATE --> POP_CHARGES
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:22-70](), [src/torchani.cpp:372-563](), [include/build_tensors.h]()

### Model Loading and JIT Compilation

The system uses PyTorch's JIT compilation to convert Python models into optimized `.pt` files that can be loaded by the C++ runtime:

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "JIT Compilation Phase"
        PYTHON_MODELS["Python ANI Models<br/>torchani.models.*"]
        JIT_SCRIPT["torch.jit.script()"]
        JIT_SAVE["torch.jit.save()"]
        PT_FILES[".pt Model Files<br/>ani1x.pt, ani2x.pt"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime Loading"
        TORCHANI_INIT["torchani_initialize()"]
        JIT_LOAD["torch::jit::load()"]
        MODEL_CONFIG["Model Configuration<br/>set_active_members()"]
        DTYPE_CAST["model.to(config.dtype())"]
    end
    
    PYTHON_MODELS --> JIT_SCRIPT
    JIT_SCRIPT --> JIT_SAVE
    JIT_SAVE --> PT_FILES
    
    PT_FILES --> TORCHANI_INIT
    TORCHANI_INIT --> JIT_LOAD
    JIT_LOAD --> MODEL_CONFIG
    MODEL_CONFIG --> DTYPE_CAST
```

**Sources:** [jit/jit.py:76-93](), [src/torchani.cpp:485-558]()

## Integration Workflows

### Full-ML Simulation Workflow

For simulations where the entire system potential is computed by neural networks:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AMBER as "Amber (sander/pmemd)"
    participant EXTPOT as "External Potential"
    participant TORCHANI as "torchani_calc_energy_force()"
    participant MODEL as "torch::jit::Module"
    
    AMBER->>EXTPOT: "Coordinates + Configuration"
    EXTPOT->>TORCHANI: "torchani_calc_energy_force()"
    TORCHANI->>MODEL: "setup_inputs_pbc() + model.forward()"
    MODEL->>TORCHANI: "Energy + Forces Tensors"
    TORCHANI->>EXTPOT: "Forces + Potential Energy"
    EXTPOT->>AMBER: "Energy/Force Values"
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:645-702](), [README.md:116-169]()

### ML/MM Simulation Workflow

For hybrid simulations with quantum and classical regions:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant AMBER as "Amber sander"
    participant QMMM as "QM/MM Interface"
    participant TORCHANI as "torchani_energy_force_with_coupling()"
    participant ELECTRO as "electro.h (Coupling)"
    
    AMBER->>QMMM: "QM Region + MM Environment"
    QMMM->>TORCHANI: "QM coords + MM charges"
    TORCHANI->>TORCHANI: "ene_pot_invacuo = model.forward()"
    TORCHANI->>ELECTRO: "coulombic_embedding_energy()"
    ELECTRO->>TORCHANI: "Coupling Energy"
    TORCHANI->>QMMM: "Total Energy + Forces"
    QMMM->>AMBER: "Combined ML/MM Potential"
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:730-833](), [include/electro.h](), [README.md:172-257]()

## Key Capabilities

### Supported Neural Network Models

The system supports multiple neural network potentials through the `torchani_builtin_models` vector:

| Model Family | Variants | Elements Supported |
|--------------|----------|--------------------|
| ANI-1x | `ani1x`, `ani1x-infer` | H, C, N, O |
| ANI-2x | `ani2x`, `ani2x-infer` | H, C, N, O, F, Cl, S |
| ANI-1ccx | `ani1ccx`, `ani1ccx-infer` | H, C, N, O |
| AimNet2 | `aimnet2-*-dsf/ewald/nocut` | Multiple variants |
| NutMeg | `nutmeg-small/medium/large` | Condensed phase systems |

### Runtime Configuration

The `GlobalConfig` class manages critical runtime parameters:

- **Device Selection**: CPU vs CUDA device configuration
- **Precision Control**: Float32 vs Float64 tensor operations  
- **PBC Support**: Periodic boundary condition handling
- **Atom Masking**: Selective evaluation for efficiency

### Performance Features

- **cuAEV Extension**: CUDA-accelerated atomic environment vectors via `use_cuaev`
- **External Neighborlists**: Amber-managed neighbor lists through `use_amber_neighborlist`
- **JIT Optimizations**: Disabled for accuracy via `torch::jit::setGraphExecutorOptimize(false)`
- **Ensemble Support**: Multiple network evaluation for uncertainty quantification

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:34-69](), [src/torchani.cpp:474-539](), [include/config.h]()

# Page: Getting Started

# Getting Started

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt)

This page provides an overview of the steps required to install, build, and configure TorchANI-Amber for your first molecular dynamics simulations. TorchANI-Amber integrates neural network potentials with the Amber molecular dynamics suite, enabling both full-ML simulations and ML/MM hybrid approaches.

For detailed installation and build instructions, see [Installation and Build](#2.1). For a complete step-by-step tutorial to run your first simulation, see [Quick Start Tutorial](#2.2). For information about the underlying architecture and API details, see [Core Architecture](#3).

## Prerequisites Overview

Before beginning the installation process, ensure you have access to the following system requirements:

| Component | Requirement | Purpose |
|-----------|-------------|---------|
| **Operating System** | Linux | Required by build system validation |
| **Compiler** | GNU GCC 11.0-13.2 | C++17 support for core libraries |
| **Python Environment** | Conda/Mamba | Dependency management |
| **CUDA Toolkit** | 12.4 | GPU acceleration (optional but recommended) |
| **Memory** | 8GB+ RAM | Model loading and tensor operations |
| **Storage** | 10GB+ free space | Dependencies and compiled libraries |

The system enforces these requirements through validation checks in the build configuration, as seen in [CMakeLists.txt:75-88]().

**Sources:** [CMakeLists.txt:75-88](), [README.md:35-37](), [environment.yaml:34-46]()

## Getting Started Workflow

The TorchANI-Amber setup process follows a structured workflow that ensures all dependencies are properly configured:

#### High-Level Installation Flow
```mermaid
graph TD
    A["Clone Repository<br/>git clone --recurse-submodules"] --> B["Create Conda Environment<br/>conda env create -f environment.yaml"]
    B --> C["Activate Environment<br/>conda activate ani-amber"]
    C --> D["Install TorchANI Python<br/>pip install torchani_sandbox_pub"]
    D --> E["Build TorchANI-Amber<br/>./run-cmake"]
    E --> F["Build Amber<br/>cmake with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH"]
    F --> G["Configure Simulation<br/>Create mdin files"]
    G --> H["Run Simulation<br/>sander/pmemd with TorchANI"]
    
    style A fill:#e1f5fe
    style E fill:#e8f5e8
    style H fill:#fff3e0
```

**Sources:** [README.md:39-83](), [CMakeLists.txt:1-12]()

## Configuration Overview

TorchANI-Amber simulations are configured through Amber's `mdin` input files using specific namelists. The configuration approach differs depending on the simulation type:

#### Simulation Configuration Patterns
```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Full-ML Configuration"
        A["&cntrl<br/>iextpot = 1"] --> B["&extpot<br/>extprog = 'TORCHANI'"]
        B --> C["&ani<br/>model_type<br/>use_cuda_device<br/>use_double_precision"]
    end
    
    subgraph "ML/MM Configuration"
        D["&cntrl<br/>ifqnt = 1"] --> E["&qmmm<br/>qm_theory = 'EXTERN'<br/>qmmask = ':1'"]
        E --> F["&ani<br/>model_type<br/>use_torchani_charges<br/>mlmm_coupling"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Available Models"
        G["ani1x<br/>ANI-1x Ensemble"]
        H["ani2x<br/>ANI-2x Ensemble"]
        I["ani1ccx<br/>ANI-1ccx Ensemble"]
        J["animbis<br/>MBIS Charge Model"]
    end
    
    C --> G
    C --> H
    C --> I
    F --> G
    F --> H
    F --> I
    F --> J
```

**Sources:** [README.md:116-169](), [README.md:172-257]()

## Environment and Dependencies

The build process relies on a carefully configured conda environment that provides all necessary dependencies:

| Dependency Category | Key Components | Purpose |
|-------------------|----------------|---------|
| **Python Runtime** | `python=3.11`, `pip>=24.0` | Core interpreter and package management |
| **PyTorch Stack** | `pytorch=2.5`, `pytorch-cuda=12.4` | Neural network backend and GPU support |
| **CUDA Toolkit** | `cuda-libraries-dev=12.4`, `cuda-nvcc=12.4` | GPU compilation and runtime |
| **Build Tools** | `cmake=3.31.1`, `gxx_linux-64=12.2` | Build system and compilers |
| **Amber Dependencies** | `fftw=3.3.10`, `netcdf-fortran=4.6.1` | MD simulation support |

The environment configuration is defined in [environment.yaml:1-68]() and automatically validated during the build process through [CMakeLists.txt:95-113]().

**Sources:** [environment.yaml:8-46](), [CMakeLists.txt:95-113]()

## Next Steps

To proceed with your TorchANI-Amber installation and setup:

1. **Installation**: Follow the detailed build instructions in [Installation and Build](#2.1), which covers environment setup, dependency resolution, and compilation of all required libraries.

2. **First Simulation**: Complete the hands-on tutorial in [Quick Start Tutorial](#2.2) to configure and run your first simulation with step-by-step guidance.

3. **Advanced Configuration**: For detailed information about simulation parameters, model options, and ML/MM setup, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1).

4. **Performance Optimization**: To benchmark your installation and optimize performance, consult the [Benchmarking System](#5) documentation.

The build process typically takes 15-30 minutes depending on your system specifications and whether you're using GPU acceleration. Ensure you have a stable internet connection for downloading dependencies during the conda environment creation phase.

**Sources:** [README.md:29-95](), [CMakeLists.txt:214-224]()

This document provides comprehensive instructions for building TorchANI-Amber from source, including dependency management, environment setup, and build configuration. It covers the CMake-based build system that handles complex dependency resolution for PyTorch, CUDA, and cuDNN libraries, and produces the core shared libraries required for Amber integration.

For information about configuring and running simulations with the built libraries, see [Quick Start Tutorial](#2.2). For details about the underlying build system architecture, see [Build System Deep Dive](#6.1).

## Prerequisites and System Requirements

TorchANI-Amber requires a Linux system with specific compiler and library versions. The build system enforces strict version compatibility to ensure proper integration with PyTorch and CUDA libraries.

### System Requirements

| Component | Requirement | Notes |
|-----------|-------------|-------|
| Operating System | Linux only | Enforced by `LinuxBuild_ensure()` |
| CMake | ≥ 3.24 | Specified in `CMakeLists.txt:2` |
| Compilers | GNU 11.0-13.2 | g++, gcc, gfortran required |
| Python | 3.11 | For PyTorch integration and JIT compilation |

### Core Dependencies

| Library | Version | Purpose |
|---------|---------|---------|
| PyTorch/LibTorch | 2.5.x | Neural network backend |
| CUDA Toolkit | 12.4 | GPU acceleration |
| cuDNN | 9.1 | Deep learning primitives |

**Build Dependencies Diagram**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "System Requirements"
        Linux["Linux OS"]
        CMAKE["CMake ≥3.24"]
        GNU["GNU Compilers 11.0-13.2"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Core Libraries"
        PYTORCH["PyTorch 2.5"]
        CUDA["CUDA Toolkit 12.4"] 
        CUDNN["cuDNN 9.1"]
        PYTHON["Python 3.11"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build Outputs"
        LIBTORCHANI["libtorchani.so"]
        LIBCUAEV["libcuaev.so"]
        LIBCELLLIST["libcell_list.so"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CMake Options"
        LINK_PYTORCH["LINK_TO_PYTORCH_LIBS"]
        PREFER_CONDA["PREFER_CONDA_LIBS"]
        JIT_COMPILE["JIT_COMPILE_MODELS"]
        DOWNLOAD_LIBTORCH["DOWNLOAD_AND_INSTALL_LIBTORCH"]
    end
    
    Linux --> CMAKE
    CMAKE --> GNU
    GNU --> PYTORCH
    PYTORCH --> CUDA
    CUDA --> CUDNN
    PYTHON --> PYTORCH
    
    LINK_PYTORCH --> PYTORCH
    PREFER_CONDA --> PYTORCH
    JIT_COMPILE --> PYTHON
    DOWNLOAD_LIBTORCH --> PYTORCH
    
    PYTORCH --> LIBTORCHANI
    CUDA --> LIBCUAEV
    PYTHON --> LIBCUAEV
    PYTORCH --> LIBCELLLIST
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:47-51](), [CMakeLists.txt:74-88](), [environment.yaml:8-47]()

## Environment Setup

The recommended approach is to use the provided conda environment, which automatically handles all dependency versions and compatibility requirements.

### Conda Environment Installation

```bash
# Clone the repository with submodules
git clone --recursive https://github.com/roitberg-group/torchani-amber.git
cd torchani-amber

# Create and activate the conda environment
conda env create -f environment.yaml
conda activate ani-amber
```

The `environment.yaml` defines the `ani-amber` environment with all required dependencies, including:

- **Core Runtime**: `pytorch=2.5`, `pytorch-cuda=12.4`
- **Build Tools**: `cmake=3.31.1`, GNU compiler suite
- **CUDA Development**: `cuda-libraries-dev=12.4`, `cuda-nvcc=12.4`
- **Additional Libraries**: OpenMPI, NetCDF-Fortran for Amber integration

### Manual Dependency Installation

For custom installations without conda, ensure these components are available:

1. **PyTorch with CUDA**: Install PyTorch 2.5 compiled with CUDA 12.4 support
2. **CUDA Toolkit Development**: Full CUDA 12.4 installation with headers and nvcc
3. **cuDNN**: Version 9.1 compatible with CUDA 12.4
4. **GNU Compilers**: g++, gcc, gfortran versions 11.0-13.2

Sources: [environment.yaml:1-68](), [CMakeLists.txt:95-112]()

## Build Configuration

The build system provides extensive configuration options through CMake variables and the `run-cmake` wrapper script. The configuration process handles dependency detection, version validation, and library path setup.

### CMake Configuration Options

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `LINK_TO_PYTORCH_LIBS` | ON | Link to existing PyTorch installation |
| `DOWNLOAD_AND_INSTALL_LIBTORCH` | OFF | Download LibTorch binaries |
| `PREFER_CONDA_LIBS` | ON | Use conda environment libraries |
| `JIT_COMPILE_MODELS` | ON | Compile ANI models to TorchScript |
| `USE_CUSTOM_CUDNN` | OFF | Use custom cuDNN installation |
| `COMPILE_WITH_CXX11ABI` | OFF | Use C++11 ABI (requires LibTorch) |

### Dependency Resolution Process

**Build Configuration Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["cmake configuration"]
    
    subgraph "Environment Detection"
        CONDA_CHECK["Check CONDA_PREFIX"]
        PYTORCH_DETECT["detect_pytorch.py"]
        VERSION_VALIDATE["Validate versions"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Library Setup"
        PYTORCH_SETUP["PyTorch/LibTorch setup"]
        CUDNN_SETUP["CudnnHelper_set_*_paths()"]
        CUDA_SETUP["CudaToolkitHelper_set_*_paths()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Compilation"
        JIT_CHECK["JIT_COMPILE_MODELS?"]
        JIT_COMPILE["TorchScriptUtils_jit_compile_models()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Target Building"
        FIND_TORCH["find_package(Torch)"]
        BUILD_CUAEV["add_library(cuaev)"]
        BUILD_CELLLIST["add_library(cell_list)"]
        BUILD_TORCHANI["add_library(torchani)"]
    end
    
    START --> CONDA_CHECK
    CONDA_CHECK --> PYTORCH_DETECT
    PYTORCH_DETECT --> VERSION_VALIDATE
    VERSION_VALIDATE --> PYTORCH_SETUP
    
    PYTORCH_SETUP --> CUDNN_SETUP
    CUDNN_SETUP --> CUDA_SETUP
    CUDA_SETUP --> JIT_CHECK
    
    JIT_CHECK -->|YES| JIT_COMPILE
    JIT_CHECK -->|NO| FIND_TORCH
    JIT_COMPILE --> FIND_TORCH
    
    FIND_TORCH --> BUILD_CUAEV
    BUILD_CUAEV --> BUILD_CELLLIST
    BUILD_CELLLIST --> BUILD_TORCHANI
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:114-165](), [CMakeLists.txt:167-212](), [cmake/detect_pytorch.py]()

### Version Validation

The build system enforces exact version matching for critical dependencies:

```cpp
// Required versions from CMakeLists.txt:47-51
REQUIRED_TORCH_VERSION = "2.5"
REQUIRED_CUDATK_VERSION = "12.4" 
REQUIRED_CUDNN_VERSION = "9.1"
```

Version validation occurs through the `detect_pytorch.py` script, which queries the PyTorch installation and reports version mismatches as fatal errors.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:47-51](), [CMakeLists.txt:119-150]()

## Build Process

### Using the run-cmake Script

The `run-cmake` script provides a convenient wrapper around the CMake build process with sensible defaults:

```bash
# Standard build with conda libraries
./run-cmake

# Build without running tests
./run-cmake -T

# Build only (no install)
./run-cmake -I

# Debug build
./run-cmake -g

# Use custom libraries instead of conda
./run-cmake -C
```

### Manual CMake Build

For more control over the build process:

```bash
# Configure
cmake -S. -Bbuild \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
    -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=$HOME/.local \
    -DLINK_TO_PYTORCH_LIBS=ON \
    -DPREFER_CONDA_LIBS=ON \
    -DJIT_COMPILE_MODELS=ON

# Build
cmake --build build

# Test
./build/tests

# Install
cmake --install build
```

### Build Targets

The build process creates three primary shared libraries:

| Library | Source Location | Purpose |
|---------|----------------|---------|
| `libcuaev.so` | `submodules/torchani_sandbox/torchani/csrc/` | CUDA-accelerated AEV calculations |
| `libcell_list.so` | `submodules/torchani_sandbox/torchani/csrc/` | Neighbor list generation |
| `libtorchani.so` | `src/*.cpp` | Main TorchANI interface library |

### Compilation Flags and Optimizations

The CUDA library `libcuaev.so` is built with specific optimizations:

```cpp
// From CMakeLists.txt:263-275
TORCHANI_OPT           // Enable CUDA intrinsics for math functions
-use_fast_math         // Enable fast math library
CUB_NS_QUALIFIER       // Wrapped CUB namespace for PyTorch compatibility
```

Sources: [run-cmake:1-114](), [CMakeLists.txt:234-287](), [CMakeLists.txt:289-323]()

## JIT Model Compilation

When `JIT_COMPILE_MODELS=ON` (default), the build system automatically compiles ANI neural network models to TorchScript format for optimized runtime performance.

### JIT Compilation Process

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant CMAKE as "CMake"
    participant JIT_PY as "jit/jit.py"
    participant TORCHANI as "TorchANI Python"
    participant MODELS as "Model Files"
    
    CMAKE->>JIT_PY: TorchScriptUtils_jit_compile_models()
    JIT_PY->>TORCHANI: Import model classes
    TORCHANI->>JIT_PY: Load model instances
    JIT_PY->>JIT_PY: torch.jit.script()
    JIT_PY->>MODELS: Save *.pt files
    MODELS->>CMAKE: Models available for linking
```

The JIT compilation is controlled by several options:

- `JIT_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATIONS`: Disable TorchScript optimizations
- `JIT_FORCE_RECOMPILATION`: Force recompilation of existing `.pt` files

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:215-223](), [cmake/TorchScriptUtils.cmake:1-29]()

## Installation and Library Paths

### Installation Directories

The CMake install process creates the following directory structure:

```
$CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX/
├── lib/Torchani/
│   ├── libtorchani.so
│   ├── libcuaev.so
│   └── libcell_list.so
├── include/Torchani/
│   └── torchani.h
├── share/Torchani/
│   └── Fortran/torchani.F90
└── share/cmake/Torchani/
    ├── TorchaniConfig.cmake
    ├── TorchaniConfigVersion.cmake
    └── TorchaniTargets.cmake
```

### RPATH Configuration

The build system automatically configures RPATH settings to ensure libraries can find their dependencies at runtime:

```cpp
// From CMakeLists.txt:340-364
TORCHANI_LIBRARIES_INSTALL_RPATH = {
    LIBTORCH_LIBRARY_DIR,      // PyTorch libraries
    CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR,     // CUDA runtime
    CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBDIR  // TorchANI libraries
}
```

This prevents runtime linking issues when using conda environments or custom CUDA installations.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:404-461](), [CMakeLists.txt:340-364]()

## Build Verification

### Running Tests

The build includes a comprehensive test suite using the Catch2 framework:

```bash
# Run tests after build
./build/tests

# Or use CTest
cd build && ctest
```

### Verifying Installation

Check that all libraries are properly installed and linked:

```bash
# Verify library installation
ls $HOME/.local/lib/Torchani/

# Check library dependencies
ldd $HOME/.local/lib/Torchani/libtorchani.so

# Verify CMake package detection
cmake --find-package -DNAME=Torchani -DCOMPILER_ID=GNU -DLANGUAGE=CXX
```

### Common Build Issues

| Issue | Cause | Solution |
|-------|-------|---------|
| PyTorch version mismatch | Wrong PyTorch version | Install PyTorch 2.5 exactly |
| CUDA not found | Missing CUDA development packages | Install `cuda-libraries-dev` |
| Compiler not supported | Non-GNU compiler | Use g++/gcc/gfortran 11.0-13.2 |
| cuDNN missing | cuDNN not in expected location | Set `USE_CUSTOM_CUDNN=ON` or use conda |

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:378-391](), [CMakeLists.txt:74-88](), [CMakeLists.txt:125-149]()

# Page: Quick Start Tutorial

# Quick Start Tutorial

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [ani-amber-logo-dark.png](ani-amber-logo-dark.png)
- [ani-amber-logo-light.png](ani-amber-logo-light.png)
- [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja](benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja)

</details>



This tutorial guides you through running your first molecular dynamics simulation with TorchANI-Amber, from initial setup to execution. You will learn to configure both full-ML simulations (entire system uses neural networks) and ML/MM hybrid simulations (neural networks for QM region, classical force fields for MM region).

For detailed installation procedures, see [Installation and Build](#2.1). For comprehensive configuration options, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For performance optimization, see [Benchmarking System](#5).

## Prerequisites and Environment Setup

TorchANI-Amber requires a conda environment with PyTorch, CUDA toolkit, and molecular dynamics dependencies. The system uses JIT-compiled neural network models that must be compatible with the LibTorch backend.

### Required Components

| Component | Purpose | Notes |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `environment.yaml` | Conda environment specification | Includes PyTorch, CUDA, cuDNN, GFortran |
| `run-cmake` | Build automation script | Handles CMake configuration and testing |
| Amber source | MD simulation engine | Must be compiled with TorchANI integration |
| CUDA Toolkit | GPU acceleration | Required even for CPU-only runs |

**Installation Workflow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["git clone --recurse-submodules"] --> B["conda env create -f environment.yaml"]
    B --> C["conda activate ani-amber"]
    C --> D["pip install torchani_sandbox_pub"]
    D --> E["./run-cmake"]
    E --> F["cmake amber with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH"]
    F --> G["Amber binaries with TorchANI integration"]
    
    H["environment.yaml"] --> B
    I["run-cmake script"] --> E
    J["CMakeLists.txt"] --> E
    K["Amber source"] --> F
    
    style E fill:#e1f5fe
    style G fill:#e8f5e8
```

Sources: [README.md:39-95]()

## Build Process Overview

The TorchANI-Amber build system creates shared libraries that integrate with Amber's external potential interface. The process involves compiling C++ extensions, linking PyTorch libraries, and generating JIT-compatible model files.

**Build System Components**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Source_Components"
        A["torchani_sandbox_pub/"] 
        B["src/torchani.cpp"]
        C["src/torchani.h"]
        D["src/torchani.F90"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Build_Artifacts"
        E["libtorchani.so"]
        F["libcuaev.so"] 
        G["libcell_list.so"]
        H["JIT model files (.pt)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration_Points"
        I["~/.local/lib/"]
        J["Amber CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH"]
        K["sander/pmemd binaries"]
    end
    
    A --> E
    B --> E
    C --> E
    D --> E
    A --> F
    A --> G
    A --> H
    
    E --> I
    F --> I
    G --> I
    H --> I
    
    I --> J
    J --> K
    
    style E fill:#e1f5fe
    style K fill:#e8f5e8
```

Sources: [README.md:54-95]()

## Configuration File Structure

TorchANI-Amber simulations require specific namelist configurations in `mdin` files. The structure differs between full-ML and ML/MM simulation types, with different required namelists and parameters.

### Full-ML Configuration

Full-ML simulations use the external potential interface with three required namelists:

| Namelist | Required Parameters | Purpose |
|----------|-------------------|---------|
| `&cntrl` | `iextpot = 1` | Enable external potential |
| `&extpot` | `extprog = 'TORCHANI'` | Specify TorchANI as external program |
| `&ani` | `model_type`, `use_cuda_device` | Configure neural network parameters |

**Namelist Configuration Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["mdin file"] --> B["&cntrl namelist"]
    A --> C["&extpot namelist"] 
    A --> D["&ani namelist"]
    
    B --> E["iextpot = 1"]
    C --> F["extprog = 'TORCHANI'"]
    D --> G["model_type = 'ani2x'"]
    D --> H["use_cuda_device = .true."]
    D --> I["use_double_precision = .true."]
    
    E --> J["torchani_initialize()"]
    F --> J
    G --> K["torch::jit::load()"]
    H --> L["CUDA device selection"]
    I --> M["Float64 tensor operations"]
    
    style J fill:#e1f5fe
    style K fill:#e8f5e8
```

Sources: [README.md:116-169](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:1-48]()

### ML/MM Configuration

ML/MM simulations use the QM/MM interface with different namelists:

| Namelist | Required Parameters | Purpose |
|----------|-------------------|---------|
| `&cntrl` | `ifqnt = 1` | Enable QM/MM calculations |
| `&qmmm` | `qm_theory = 'EXTERN'`, `qmmask` | Configure QM region and coupling |
| `&ani` | Standard parameters + ML/MM options | Configure neural network and coupling |

## Running Your First Simulation

### Step 1: Environment Activation

```bash
conda activate ani-amber
```

The `ani-amber` environment must be active during runtime because the compiled binaries depend on CUDA and PyTorch libraries within the conda environment.

### Step 2: Prepare Input Files

Create the standard Amber input files:
- `.prmtop` topology file
- `.inpcrd` or `.rst7` coordinate file  
- `mdin` configuration file with TorchANI namelists

### Step 3: Basic Full-ML Simulation

**Example mdin Configuration**

```
&cntrl
    iextpot = 1
    imin = 0
    nstlim = 1000
    dt = 0.002
    ntc = 2, ntf = 2
    temp0 = 300.0
    ntt = 3
/
&extpot
    extprog = "TORCHANI"
/
&ani
    model_type = "ani2x"
    use_double_precision = .true.
    use_cuda_device = .true.
    use_cuaev = .true.
/
```

**Execution Command**

```bash
sander -O -i input.mdin -p system.prmtop -c system.inpcrd -o output.mdout
```

### Step 4: Basic ML/MM Simulation

**Example mdin Configuration**

```
&cntrl
    ifqnt = 1
    imin = 0
    nstlim = 1000
    dt = 0.002
/
&qmmm
    qm_theory = 'EXTERN'
    qm_ewald = 0
    qmmm_int = 1
    qmmask = ':1'
    qmcut = 15.0
/
&ani
    model_type = 'ani2x'
    use_cuda_device = .true.
    use_torchani_charges = .false.
    mlmm_coupling = 0
/
```

Sources: [README.md:152-257]()

## Runtime Execution Flow

The following diagram shows how TorchANI-Amber integrates with Amber during simulation execution:

**Simulation Runtime Architecture**

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant U as "User Command"
    participant S as "sander/pmemd"
    participant T as "torchani_initialize()"
    participant J as "torch::jit::load()"
    participant C as "torchani_compute()"
    participant G as "GPU/CPU tensors"
    
    U->>S: "sander -i input.mdin"
    S->>T: "Parse &ani namelist"
    T->>J: "Load .pt model file"
    J->>T: "Return JIT module"
    
    loop "MD Steps"
        S->>C: "coordinates, cell, pbc"
        C->>G: "Tensor operations"
        G->>C: "energies, forces, charges"
        C->>S: "Return forces/energies"
        S->>S: "Update positions"
    end
    
    S->>U: "Write trajectory files"
```

Sources: [README.md:114-169]()

## Verification and Testing

### Quick Validation Test

Run a short simulation to verify the installation:

```bash
# Create minimal test case (10 steps)
sander -O -i test.mdin -p system.prmtop -c system.inpcrd -o test.out
```

Check for successful initialization messages in the output:
- `TorchANI initialization successful`
- `Model loaded: [model_type]`
- `Device: CUDA:0` or `Device: CPU`

### Common Issues and Solutions

| Issue | Symptom | Solution |
|-------|---------|----------|
| CUDA library missing | `libcudart.so not found` | Ensure conda environment is activated |
| Model load failure | `Could not load model` | Verify `model_type` parameter |
| Memory errors | `CUDA out of memory` | Reduce system size or use CPU |

Sources: [README.md:347-349]()

## Next Steps

After successfully running your first simulation:

1. **Performance Optimization**: Use the [Bench CLI Tool](#5.1) to optimize GPU settings and scaling
2. **Advanced Configuration**: Explore [ML/MM Setup and Coupling](#4.2) for hybrid simulations  
3. **Custom Models**: See [Model Wrappers](#3.3) for using custom neural network potentials
4. **Production Runs**: Review [Input Templates and Examples](#4.3) for simulation-specific configurations

The benchmark templates in [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:1-48]() provide examples of production-ready configurations with various performance optimizations.

Sources: [README.md:1-451](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:1-48]()

# Page: Core Architecture

# Core Architecture

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [jit/jit.py](jit/jit.py)
- [jit/make_bulk.py](jit/make_bulk.py)
- [src/build_tensors.cpp](src/build_tensors.cpp)
- [src/build_tensors.h](src/build_tensors.h)
- [src/config.h](src/config.h)
- [src/torchani.cpp](src/torchani.cpp)

</details>



This document describes the core runtime architecture of TorchANI-Amber, focusing on the C++ engine, JIT compilation system, and tensor operations that form the computational foundation. For information about build system configuration, see [Build System Deep Dive](#6.1). For API usage details, see [API Reference](#3.2). For Python model wrappers, see [Model Wrappers](#3.3).

## Global Configuration System

The architecture centers around a `GlobalConfig` class that manages device placement, precision, and computational settings throughout the system. This singleton-like configuration object ensures consistent tensor operations across all components.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "GlobalConfig Management"
        GC["GlobalConfig"] --> Device["Device Selection<br/>CPU/CUDA + Index"]
        GC --> Precision["Precision Control<br/>Float32/Float64"]
        GC --> PBC["PBC Configuration<br/>Periodic Boundaries"]
        GC --> NoEval["No-Eval Atoms<br/>Selective Evaluation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tensor Operations"
        Device --> TensorOpts["torch::TensorOptions"]
        Precision --> TensorOpts
        TensorOpts --> TensorConv["Tensor Conversion<br/>tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime Usage"
        TensorConv --> ModelExec["Model Execution"]
        NoEval --> AtomMasking["Selective Atom Processing"]
        PBC --> BoundaryHandling["Periodic Boundary Logic"]
    end
```

**Configuration Management Overview**
Sources: [src/config.h:1-65](), [src/torchani.cpp:23-26]()

The `GlobalConfig` class provides centralized control over:
- **Device Management**: CPU vs CUDA device selection with device indexing
- **Precision Control**: Float32 vs Float64 precision for all tensor operations  
- **PBC Handling**: Automatic periodic boundary condition tensor creation
- **Selective Evaluation**: Support for excluding specific atoms from neural network evaluation

Key methods include `set_device_and_precision()` for initialization and `tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device()` for consistent tensor conversion throughout the pipeline.

## JIT Compilation Pipeline

The system uses a sophisticated JIT compilation pipeline that converts Python-based neural network models into optimized `.pt` files for C++ execution.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Model Sources"
        TorchANI["TorchANI Models<br/>ANI1x, ANI2x, etc."]
        AimNet2["AimNet2 Models<br/>Various functionals"]
        Nutmeg["Nutmeg Models<br/>Small/Medium/Large"]
    end
    
    subgraph "JIT Compilation Process"
        ModelSpec["ModelSpec<br/>cls, infer, kwargs"]
        InstantiatePy["Python Model<br/>Instantiation"]
        OptimDisable["Optimization Disable<br/>_disable_jit_optimizations()"]
        JITScript["torch.jit.script()"]
        JITSave["torch.jit.save()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Files"
        PTFiles[".pt Files<br/>JIT-compiled models"]
        ModelRegistry["Built-in Model Registry<br/>torchani_builtin_models"]
    end
    
    TorchANI --> ModelSpec
    AimNet2 --> ModelSpec
    Nutmeg --> ModelSpec
    
    ModelSpec --> InstantiatePy
    InstantiatePy --> OptimDisable
    OptimDisable --> JITScript
    JITScript --> JITSave
    JITSave --> PTFiles
    PTFiles --> ModelRegistry
```

**JIT Compilation System**
Sources: [jit/jit.py:1-180](), [src/torchani.cpp:34-69](), [src/torchani.cpp:475-478]()

The compilation process involves:

1. **Model Specification**: `ModelSpec` dataclass defines model class, inference mode, and compilation kwargs
2. **Selective Compilation**: Only compiles missing `.pt` files unless force recompilation is requested
3. **Optimization Control**: Disables various PyTorch JIT optimizations to ensure numerical accuracy
4. **Registry Management**: Maintains `torchani_builtin_models` vector with all available model names
5. **Error Handling**: Graceful fallback for models that fail compilation

The system supports both training and inference-optimized model variants, with inference models using `to_infer_model()` for reduced memory usage.

## Tensor Building and Data Conversion

A critical architectural component handles conversion between raw C/Fortran buffers and PyTorch tensors with proper device placement and gradient tracking.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Buffers"
        CoordsBuffer["coords_buf[][3]<br/>double arrays"]
        CellBuffer["cell_buf[][3]<br/>3x3 cell matrix"]
        NeighborBuffer["neighborlist_buf[2]<br/>int arrays"]
        ShiftsBuffer["shifts_buf[][3]<br/>shift vectors"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Tensor Conversion Functions"
        DBLCoords["dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()"]
        DBLCell["dbl_buf_to_cell_tensor()"]
        INTNeighbor["int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor()"]
        DBLShifts["dbl_buf_to_shifts_tensor()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "PyTorch Tensors"
        CoordsTensor["coords tensor<br/>requires_grad=true<br/>batch dimension added"]
        CellTensor["cell tensor<br/>device/dtype converted"]
        NeighborTensor["neighborlist tensor<br/>int32->int64 conversion"]
        ShiftsTensor["shifts tensor<br/>requires_grad=true"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Input Preparation"
        SetupInputs["setup_inputs_*()<br/>functions"]
        IValueVectors["std::vector<torch::jit::IValue>"]
    end
    
    CoordsBuffer --> DBLCoords
    CellBuffer --> DBLCell
    NeighborBuffer --> INTNeighbor
    ShiftsBuffer --> DBLShifts
    
    DBLCoords --> CoordsTensor
    DBLCell --> CellTensor
    INTNeighbor --> NeighborTensor
    DBLShifts --> ShiftsTensor
    
    CoordsTensor --> SetupInputs
    CellTensor --> SetupInputs
    NeighborTensor --> SetupInputs
    ShiftsTensor --> SetupInputs
    
    SetupInputs --> IValueVectors
```

**Tensor Building Architecture**
Sources: [src/build_tensors.cpp:1-71](), [src/build_tensors.h:1-46](), [src/torchani.cpp:72-153]()

Key tensor conversion functions:

| Function | Purpose | Special Handling |
|----------|---------|-----------------|
| `dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()` | Coordinate conversion | Adds batch dimension, enables gradients |
| `dbl_buf_to_cell_tensor()` | Unit cell conversion | 3x3 matrix handling |
| `int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor()` | Neighbor list conversion | int32 → int64 widening |
| `dbl_buf_to_shifts_tensor()` | Shift vector conversion | Gradient tracking enabled |

All conversion functions use the global `GlobalConfig` to ensure consistent device placement and dtype conversion via `tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device()`.

## Model Loading and Execution Engine

The core execution engine manages JIT model loading, method resolution, and configuration for different computational scenarios.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Model Loading"
        ModelPath["Model Path Resolution<br/>Built-in vs Custom"]
        JITLoad["torch::jit::load()"]
        ModelConfig["Model Configuration<br/>Precision, Device, Strategy"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Configuration"
        NetworkIdx["set_active_members()<br/>Network Selection"]
        Strategy["set_strategy()<br/>cuaev vs pyaev"]
        ExtraFeatures["set_extra_features()<br/>Nutmeg features"]
        Precision["model.to(dtype)"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Pathways"
        StandardForward["model.forward()<br/>Standard execution"]
        ExternalNeighbors["compute_from_external_neighbors()<br/>Custom neighbor lists"]
        MethodValidation["validate_model_output()<br/>Output validation"]
    end
    
    ModelPath --> JITLoad
    JITLoad --> ModelConfig
    ModelConfig --> NetworkIdx
    ModelConfig --> Strategy
    ModelConfig --> ExtraFeatures
    ModelConfig --> Precision
    
    ModelConfig --> StandardForward
    ModelConfig --> ExternalNeighbors
    StandardForward --> MethodValidation
    ExternalNeighbors --> MethodValidation
```

**Model Execution Architecture**
Sources: [src/torchani.cpp:371-563](), [src/torchani.cpp:621-635](), [src/torchani.cpp:688-701]()

The execution engine provides:

1. **Dynamic Model Loading**: Resolves built-in model names to file paths or accepts custom paths
2. **Method-Based Configuration**: Uses optional model methods for runtime configuration
3. **Execution Strategy Selection**: Supports both standard neighbor computation and external neighbor lists
4. **Output Validation**: Ensures model outputs match expected tuple structure

Key execution optimizations include disabling TF32/FP16 for numerical accuracy and JIT graph optimizations for deterministic behavior.

## Computation Pathways

The system supports multiple computation pathways depending on simulation requirements and model capabilities.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Classification"
        HasPBC{{"Periodic Boundaries?"}}
        OnlyBonded{{"Only Bonded Interactions?"}}
        HasExternalNL{{"External Neighbor List?"}}
        UseCharges{{"Predict/Use Charges?"}}
    end
    
    subgraph "Pathway Selection"
        StandardPBC["setup_inputs_pbc()"]
        StandardNoPBC["setup_inputs_nopbc()"]
        BondedPBC["setup_inputs_only_bonded_pbc()"]
        BondedNoPBC["setup_inputs_only_bonded_nopbc()"]
        ExternalNL["torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output Processing"
        ForceCalc["calculate_and_populate_forces()"]
        EnergyPop["populate_potential_energy()"]
        ChargePop["populate_atomic_charges()"]
        QBCCalc["calc_qbcs()<br/>Uncertainty quantification"]
    end
    
    HasPBC -->|Yes| HasExternalNL
    HasPBC -->|No| OnlyBonded
    
    HasExternalNL -->|Yes| ExternalNL
    HasExternalNL -->|No| OnlyBonded
    
    OnlyBonded -->|Yes + PBC| BondedPBC
    OnlyBonded -->|Yes + No PBC| BondedNoPBC
    OnlyBonded -->|No + PBC| StandardPBC
    OnlyBonded -->|No + No PBC| StandardNoPBC
    
    StandardPBC --> ForceCalc
    StandardNoPBC --> ForceCalc
    BondedPBC --> ForceCalc
    BondedNoPBC --> ForceCalc
    ExternalNL --> ForceCalc
    
    ForceCalc --> EnergyPop
    EnergyPop --> ChargePop
    ChargePop --> QBCCalc
```

**Computation Pathway Architecture**
Sources: [src/torchani.cpp:645-702](), [src/torchani.cpp:704-722](), [src/torchani.cpp:859-879](), [src/torchani.cpp:881-916]()

Available computation pathways:

| Function | Use Case | Key Features |
|----------|----------|-------------|
| `torchani_calc_energy_force()` | Standard MD | PBC support, bonded-only option |
| `torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors()` | Custom neighbor lists | External neighbor list input |
| `torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges()` | Charge prediction | Charge output with derivatives |
| `torchani_energy_force_with_coupling()` | QM/MM embedding | Environmental charge coupling |
| `torchani_energy_force_qbc()` | Uncertainty quantification | Ensemble standard deviation |
| `torchani_data_for_monitored_mlmm()` | Advanced QM/MM | Combined charge and QBC derivatives |

Each pathway handles automatic differentiation for force calculation via `torch::autograd::grad()` and includes unit conversion from Hartree to kcal/mol using the constant `HARTREE_TO_KCALMOL = 627.5094738898777`.

Sources: [src/torchani.cpp:1-918](), [src/config.h:1-65](), [src/build_tensors.cpp:1-71](), [src/build_tensors.h:1-46](), [jit/jit.py:1-180]()

# Page: C++ Engine and JIT System

# C++ Engine and JIT System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [jit/jit.py](jit/jit.py)
- [jit/make_bulk.py](jit/make_bulk.py)
- [src/build_tensors.cpp](src/build_tensors.cpp)
- [src/build_tensors.h](src/build_tensors.h)
- [src/config.h](src/config.h)
- [src/torchani.cpp](src/torchani.cpp)

</details>



## Purpose and Scope

This document covers the core C++ implementation that powers TorchANI-Amber's neural network potential calculations and the JIT (Just-In-Time) compilation system that prepares PyTorch models for high-performance execution. The C++ engine handles tensor operations, automatic differentiation for force calculations, and interfaces with PyTorch's LibTorch backend for model inference.

For information about the C and Fortran API interfaces that wrap this engine, see [API Reference](#3.2). For details about Python model wrappers, see [Model Wrappers](#3.3).

## JIT Compilation System

The JIT compilation system transforms PyTorch models into optimized `.pt` files that can be loaded and executed efficiently by the C++ engine. This system is implemented primarily in Python and handles the compilation of various neural network potential models.

### JIT Compilation Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["`jit.py script`"] --> B["`_check_which_models_need_compilation()`"]
    B --> C{"`Models need compilation?`"}
    C -->|No| D["`Exit: nothing to compile`"]
    C -->|Yes| E["`Import torch and torchani`"]
    E --> F["`_disable_jit_optimizations()`"]
    F --> G["`ModelSpec creation`"]
    G --> H["`_jit_compile_and_save_models_in_spec()`"]
    H --> I["`getattr(torchani.models, spec.cls)`"]
    I --> J["`torch.jit.script(model)`"]
    J --> K["`torch.jit.save(.pt file)`"]
    K --> L["`Model ready for C++ loading`"]
    
    M["`Built-in models`"] --> N["`ani1x, ani2x, aimnet2, nutmeg`"]
    N --> G
    
    O["`External models`"] --> P["`Custom .pt paths`"]
    P --> G
```

**Sources:** [jit/jit.py:1-180]()

### Model Compilation Process

The `ModelSpec` class defines the compilation parameters for each model:

| Property | Description | Usage |
|----------|-------------|--------|
| `cls` | Model class name | Maps to `torchani.models` attributes |
| `infer` | Inference-only optimization | Reduces model size for deployment |
| `kwargs` | Model parameters | Sets neighborlist and strategy options |

The compilation process involves several key functions:

- `_jit_compile_and_save_models_in_spec()` - Core compilation logic
- `_reset_jit_registry()` - Clears PyTorch JIT state between compilations
- `_disable_jit_optimizations()` - Prevents optimization bugs during compilation

**Sources:** [jit/jit.py:15-93]()

## C++ Engine Core

The C++ engine is the performance-critical component that loads JIT-compiled models and executes neural network calculations. It manages global state, coordinates tensor operations, and handles automatic differentiation for force calculations.

### Engine Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["`torchani_initialize()`"] --> B["`GlobalConfig config`"]
    A --> C["`torch::jit::Module model`"]
    A --> D["`torchani_atomic_numbers`"]
    
    B --> E["`Device/precision setup`"]
    C --> F["`torch::jit::load(.pt file)`"]
    D --> G["`Atomic number tensors`"]
    
    H["`Calculation Functions`"] --> I["`torchani_calc_energy_force()`"]
    H --> J["`torchani_energy_force_with_coupling()`"]
    H --> K["`torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors()`"]
    
    I --> L["`setup_inputs_pbc/nopbc()`"]
    J --> L
    K --> L
    
    L --> M["`model.forward(inputs)`"]
    M --> N["`calculate_and_populate_forces()`"]
    M --> O["`populate_potential_energy()`"]
    
    P["`Tensor Building`"] --> Q["`dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()`"]
    P --> R["`int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor()`"]
    Q --> L
    R --> L
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:22-70](), [src/torchani.cpp:371-563]()

### Global State Management

The engine maintains several global variables that persist across function calls:

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GlobalState {
        +GlobalConfig config
        +torch::jit::Module model
        +torch::Tensor torchani_atomic_numbers
        +torch::Tensor torchani_do_eval_atoms_mask
        +torch::Tensor torchani_do_eval_idxs
        +double HARTREE_TO_KCALMOL
        +vector~string~ torchani_builtin_models
    }
    
    class GlobalConfig {
        -torch::TensorOptions m_opts
        -bool m_use_no_eval_atoms
        +dtype()
        +device()
        +set_device_and_precision()
        +tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device()
        +enabled_pbc()
    }
    
    GlobalState --> GlobalConfig
```

The `GlobalConfig` class encapsulates device and precision settings, providing methods to convert tensors to the appropriate format for model execution.

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:22-32](), [src/config.h:12-64]()

## Tensor Building System

The tensor building system converts C-style arrays from Amber into PyTorch tensors with proper device placement, data types, and gradient requirements. This system is crucial for bridging Amber's memory layout with PyTorch's tensor operations.

### Tensor Conversion Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["`C arrays from Amber`"] --> B["`torch::from_blob()`"]
    B --> C["`Type conversion`"]
    C --> D["`Device placement`"]
    D --> E["`Gradient setup`"]
    E --> F["`Batch dimension`"]
    F --> G["`PyTorch tensors`"]
    
    H["`dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()`"] --> I["`3D coordinates`"]
    J["`int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor()`"] --> K["`Neighbor indices`"]
    L["`dbl_buf_to_cell_tensor()`"] --> M["`Unit cell vectors`"]
    
    I --> G
    K --> G
    M --> G
```

**Sources:** [src/build_tensors.cpp:18-70]()

### Key Tensor Building Functions

| Function | Input | Output | Purpose |
|----------|-------|--------|---------|
| `dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor()` | `double coords[][3]` | `torch::Tensor` | Atomic coordinates with gradients |
| `int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor()` | `int* neighborlist[2]` | `torch::Tensor` | Neighbor pair indices |
| `dbl_buf_to_cell_tensor()` | `double cell[][3]` | `torch::Tensor` | Periodic cell vectors |
| `dbl_buf_to_tensor()` | `void* buf` | `torch::Tensor` | Generic tensor conversion |

The coordinate tensors are marked with `requires_grad_(true)` to enable automatic differentiation for force calculations.

**Sources:** [src/build_tensors.h:12-45]()

## Force and Energy Calculations

The engine provides multiple calculation pathways for different simulation scenarios, each optimized for specific use cases.

### Calculation Function Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["`Input Setup`"] --> B["`setup_inputs_pbc()`"]
    A --> C["`setup_inputs_nopbc()`"]
    A --> D["`setup_inputs_only_bonded_pbc()`"]
    
    B --> E["`model.forward(inputs)`"]
    C --> E
    D --> E
    
    E --> F["`validate_model_output()`"]
    F --> G["`torch::autograd::grad()`"]
    G --> H["`calculate_and_populate_forces()`"]
    
    I["`Energy Extraction`"] --> J["`output.toTuple()->elements()[1]`"]
    J --> K["`populate_potential_energy()`"]
    
    L["`Charge Calculations`"] --> M["`calculate_and_populate_charge_derivatives()`"]
    L --> N["`populate_atomic_charges()`"]
```

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:72-153](), [src/torchani.cpp:250-298]()

### Force Calculation Process

The force calculation uses PyTorch's automatic differentiation:

1. **Setup**: Coordinates are wrapped in tensors with `requires_grad=True`
2. **Forward Pass**: Model computes energy from coordinates
3. **Backward Pass**: `torch::autograd::grad()` computes energy derivatives
4. **Force Extraction**: Forces = negative gradient × unit conversion factor
5. **Memory Transfer**: Results copied back to C arrays for Amber

The `HARTREE_TO_KCALMOL` constant (627.5094738898777) converts from atomic units to kcal/mol.

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:250-298](), [src/torchani.cpp:31]()

## Model Integration and Validation

The engine includes robust model loading, validation, and configuration management to ensure compatibility with different neural network potential models.

### Model Loading and Configuration

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["`torchani_initialize()`"] --> B{"`Built-in model?`"}
    B -->|Yes| C["`Construct path from jit_models_dir`"]
    B -->|No| D["`Use provided path directly`"]
    
    C --> E["`Check model subdirectory`"]
    E --> F["`aimnet2/`, `nutmeg/`, or root`"]
    F --> G["`torch::jit::load(model_path)`"]
    D --> G
    
    G --> H["`model.to(config.dtype())`"]
    H --> I["`Configure model methods`"]
    I --> J["`set_active_members(network_index)`"]
    I --> K["`set_strategy(cuaev/pyaev)`"]
    I --> L["`set_extra_features(file_data)`"]
    
    M["`JIT Optimizations`"] --> N["`torch::jit::setGraphExecutorOptimize(false)`"]
    N --> O["`Disable TF32, FP16 for accuracy`"]
```

The built-in model list includes ANI, AimNet2, and NutMeg variants, with automatic path resolution based on model type.

**Sources:** [src/torchani.cpp:389-562](), [src/torchani.cpp:34-69]()

## Configuration Management

The `GlobalConfig` class centralizes device and precision management, ensuring consistent tensor operations across the entire engine.

### Configuration System

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class GlobalConfig {
        -torch::TensorOptions m_opts
        -bool m_use_no_eval_atoms
        +set_device_and_precision(use_cuda, device_idx, use_double)
        +tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device(tensor)
        +enabled_pbc()
        +device()
        +dtype()
    }
    
    class TensorOperations {
        +dbl_buf_to_coords_tensor(config, coords, num_atoms)
        +int_buf_to_neighborlist_tensor(config, neighborlist, num_neighbors)
        +config.tensor_to_torchani_dtype_and_device(tensor)
    }
    
    GlobalConfig --> TensorOperations : "configures"
```

The configuration system handles:
- **Device Selection**: CPU vs CUDA with specific device indices
- **Precision Management**: Float32 vs Float64 for different accuracy requirements
- **PBC Settings**: Automatic periodic boundary condition tensor generation
- **Atom Masking**: Support for excluding atoms from neural network evaluation

**Sources:** [src/config.h:9-64]()

# Page: API Reference

# API Reference

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [.gitmodules](.gitmodules)
- [include/torchani.h](include/torchani.h)
- [src-fortran/torchani.F90](src-fortran/torchani.F90)
- [tests/tests.cpp](tests/tests.cpp)

</details>



This document provides a complete reference for the C and Fortran APIs that enable integration of TorchANI neural network potentials with Amber molecular dynamics simulations. The APIs handle model initialization, energy and force calculations, charge predictions, and ML/MM coupling for various simulation scenarios.

For information about the underlying C++ engine implementation, see [C++ Engine and JIT System](#3.1). For simulation configuration details, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1).

## API Architecture Overview

The TorchANI-Amber API is structured in two layers: a core C interface that directly wraps the C++ implementation, and a Fortran interface that provides both direct bindings and convenience wrappers for Amber integration.

**API Layer Architecture**

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Amber Integration Layer"
        SANDER["sander/pmemd MD Engines"]
        AMBER_CALLS["Amber Force Calculations"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Fortran Interface Layer"
        FORTRAN_API["torchani.F90<br/>Fortran Module"]
        FORTRAN_WRAPPERS["Convenience Wrappers<br/>torchani_energy_force<br/>torchani_energy_force_pbc"]
        FORTRAN_DIRECT["Direct Bindings<br/>torchani_calc_energy_force<br/>torchani_initialize"]
    end
    
    subgraph "C Interface Layer"
        C_API["torchani.h<br/>C External Interface"]
        INIT_FUNC["torchani_initialize"]
        CALC_FUNC["torchani_calc_energy_force"]
        CHARGES_FUNC["torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges"]
        COUPLING_FUNC["torchani_energy_force_with_coupling"]
    end
    
    subgraph "C++ Engine"
        CPP_IMPL["torchani.cpp<br/>Implementation"]
        PYTORCH["PyTorch JIT Runtime"]
    end
    
    AMBER_CALLS --> FORTRAN_WRAPPERS
    AMBER_CALLS --> FORTRAN_DIRECT
    FORTRAN_WRAPPERS --> FORTRAN_DIRECT
    FORTRAN_DIRECT --> C_API
    
    C_API --> INIT_FUNC
    C_API --> CALC_FUNC
    C_API --> CHARGES_FUNC
    C_API --> COUPLING_FUNC
    
    INIT_FUNC --> CPP_IMPL
    CALC_FUNC --> CPP_IMPL
    CHARGES_FUNC --> CPP_IMPL
    COUPLING_FUNC --> CPP_IMPL
    
    CPP_IMPL --> PYTORCH
```

Sources: [include/torchani.h:1-109](), [src-fortran/torchani.F90:1-782]()

## C API Reference

The C API provides the core interface functions for model initialization and various types of energy/force calculations. All functions use C-compatible data types and follow C calling conventions.

### Initialization Function

**`torchani_initialize`**

Initializes a TorchANI model for subsequent energy and force calculations.

```c
void torchani_initialize(
    int num_atoms,
    int atomic_nums[],      // Shape (num_atoms,)
    int no_eval_atoms[],    // Shape (num_atoms,)
    const char* model_type,
    int device_index,
    int network_index,
    bool use_double_precision,
    bool use_cuda_device,
    bool use_cuaev
);
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `num_atoms` | `int` | Total number of atoms in the system |
| `atomic_nums` | `int[]` | Array of atomic numbers for each atom |
| `no_eval_atoms` | `int[]` | Mask array: 1 = skip evaluation, 0 = evaluate |
| `model_type` | `const char*` | Model name: "ani1x", "ani1ccx", "ani2x", "animbis" |
| `device_index` | `int` | CUDA device index (0 for first GPU, ignored for CPU) |
| `network_index` | `int` | Network ensemble index (-1 for all networks) |
| `use_double_precision` | `bool` | Use double precision calculations |
| `use_cuda_device` | `bool` | Enable CUDA acceleration |
| `use_cuaev` | `bool` | Use CUDA-accelerated AEV calculations |

Sources: [include/torchani.h:4-14]()

### Core Energy and Force Functions

**`torchani_calc_energy_force`**

Calculates energy and forces for a molecular system with optional periodic boundary conditions.

```c
void torchani_calc_energy_force(
    int num_atoms,
    double coords[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double cell[][3],          // Shape (3, 3)
    bool use_pbc,
    int* molecule_idxs_buf,    // Shape (num_atoms,)
    bool calc_only_bonded,
    int net_charge,
    /* outputs */
    double forces[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double* potential_energy   // Scalar
);
```

**`torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors`**

Calculates energy and forces using a pre-computed neighbor list, typically from Amber's neighbor list generation.

```c
void torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors(
    int num_atoms,
    int num_neighbors,
    double coords[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    int* neighborlist[2],      // Shape (2, num_neighbors)
    double shifts[][3],        // Shape (num_neighbors, 3)
    int* molecule_idxs_buf,    // Shape (num_atoms,)
    bool calc_only_bonded,
    int net_charge,
    /* outputs */
    double forces[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double* potential_energy
);
```

Sources: [include/torchani.h:16-41]()

### Charge Prediction Functions

**`torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges`**

Calculates energy, forces, and atomic charges for charge-capable models like animbis.

```c
void torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges(
    int num_atoms,
    double coords[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    /* outputs */
    double forces[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double atomic_charges[],   // Shape (num_atoms,)
    double* potential_energy   // Scalar
);
```

**`torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges_with_derivatives`**

Extended charge calculation that also provides charge derivatives for ML/MM coupling.

```c
void torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges_with_derivatives(
    int num_atoms,
    double coords[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    /* outputs */
    double forces[][3],        // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double atomic_charges[],   // Shape (num_atoms,)
    double* atomic_charges_grad,  // Shape (num_atoms, num_atoms, 3)
    double* potential_energy   // Scalar
);
```

The `atomic_charges_grad` array stores derivatives where element `[i, j, k]` represents the derivative of the charge on atom `k` with respect to the `i`-th coordinate of atom `j`.

Sources: [include/torchani.h:43-64]()

### ML/MM Coupling Functions

**`torchani_energy_force_with_coupling`**

Performs energy and force calculations with electrostatic coupling to external point charges for ML/MM simulations.

```c
void torchani_energy_force_with_coupling(
    int num_atoms,
    int num_env_charges,
    double distortion_k,
    double coords_buf[][3],
    double atomic_alphas_buf[],        // Shape (num_atoms,)
    double env_charge_coords_buf[][3], // Shape (num_env_charges, 3)
    double env_charges_buf[],          // Shape (num_env_charges,)
    bool predict_charges,
    bool use_simple_polarization_correction,
    bool use_charge_derivatives,
    /* outputs */
    double forces_on_atoms_buf[][3],     // Shape (num_atoms, 3)
    double forces_on_env_charges_buf[][3], // Shape (num_env_charges, 3)
    double atomic_charges_buf[],         // Shape (num_atoms,)
    double* ene_pot_invacuo_buf,
    double* ene_pot_embed_pol_buf,
    double* ene_pot_embed_dist_buf,
    double* ene_pot_embed_coulomb_buf,
    double* ene_pot_total_buf
);
```

This function decomposes the total potential energy into vacuum, polarization, distortion, and Coulomb embedding components for detailed analysis of ML/MM interactions.

Sources: [include/torchani.h:87-107]()

### Key Fortran Wrapper Functions

**`torchani_initialize`**

High-level Fortran wrapper for model initialization with automatic array size detection and type conversion.

```fortran
subroutine torchani_initialize(
    atomic_nums,
    no_eval_atoms,
    device_index,
    model_type,
    network_index,
    use_double_precision,
    use_cuda_device,
    use_cuaev
)
```

**`torchani_energy_force`**

Simplified energy/force calculation for non-periodic systems.

```fortran
subroutine torchani_energy_force(
    num_atoms,
    coords,
    forces,
    potential_energy
)
```

**`torchani_energy_force_pbc`**

Energy/force calculation with periodic boundary conditions.

```fortran
subroutine torchani_energy_force_pbc(
    num_atoms,
    coords,
    cell,
    forces,
    potential_energy
)
```

Sources: [src-fortran/torchani.F90:283-543]()

### Neighbor List Conversion Utilities

The Fortran interface provides specialized functions to convert Amber's neighbor list formats to the format expected by TorchANI.

**`convert_sander_neighborlist_to_ani_fmt`**

Converts sander's image-based neighbor list to TorchANI format.

**`convert_pmemd_neighborlist_to_ani_fmt`**

Converts pmemd's neighbor list format to TorchANI format.

These utilities handle the complex mapping between Amber's internal neighbor representations and TorchANI's expectations, including proper handling of periodic boundary conditions and translation vectors.

Sources: [src-fortran/torchani.F90:591-713]()

## Function Call Flow Patterns

**Typical API Usage Flow**

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["Simulation Start"]
    INIT["torchani_initialize<br/>• Load model<br/>• Set device/precision<br/>• Initialize tensors"]
    
    subgraph "MD Loop"
        COORDS["Update Coordinates"]
        NEIGHBORS["Generate Neighbor List<br/>(Optional)"]
        CALC_CHOICE{"Calculation Type"}
        
        BASIC_CALC["torchani_calc_energy_force<br/>Basic E&F calculation"]
        NEIGHBOR_CALC["torchani_calc_energy_force_from_external_neighbors<br/>Use pre-computed neighbors"]
        CHARGES_CALC["torchani_energy_force_atomic_charges<br/>E&F with charges"]
        COUPLING_CALC["torchani_energy_force_with_coupling<br/>ML/MM coupling"]
        
        UPDATE_FORCES["Update Forces in MD"]
    end
    
    START --> INIT
    INIT --> COORDS
    COORDS --> NEIGHBORS
    NEIGHBORS --> CALC_CHOICE
    
    CALC_CHOICE --> BASIC_CALC
    CALC_CHOICE --> NEIGHBOR_CALC
    CALC_CHOICE --> CHARGES_CALC
    CALC_CHOICE --> COUPLING_CALC
    
    BASIC_CALC --> UPDATE_FORCES
    NEIGHBOR_CALC --> UPDATE_FORCES
    CHARGES_CALC --> UPDATE_FORCES
    COUPLING_CALC --> UPDATE_FORCES
    
    UPDATE_FORCES --> COORDS
```

Sources: [tests/tests.cpp:94-146](), [include/torchani.h:4-107]()

## Parameter Specifications

### Model Types

| Model Type | Description | Charge Prediction | Elements Supported |
|------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| `"ani1x"` | ANI-1x model | No | H, C, N, O |
| `"ani1ccx"` | ANI-1ccx model | No | H, C, N, O |
| `"ani2x"` | ANI-2x model | No | H, C, N, O |
| `"animbis"` | ANI with MBIS charges | Yes | H, C, N, O |

### Array Layouts and Memory Management

- **Coordinates**: Row-major layout `coords[atom_idx][xyz]`
- **Forces**: Row-major layout `forces[atom_idx][xyz]`
- **Cell matrix**: Row-major layout `cell[3][3]` representing unit cell vectors
- **Neighbor lists**: Format `neighborlist[pair_idx][atom1/atom2]`
- **Charge derivatives**: Layout `[num_atoms, num_atoms, 3]` with Fortran ordering

### Boolean Parameter Conventions

The C API uses C99 `bool` types, while the Fortran interface automatically converts between Fortran logical types and C boolean types using the `fbool_to_cbool` utility function.

Sources: [include/torchani.h:1-109](), [src-fortran/torchani.F90:733-740]()

# Page: Model Wrappers

# Model Wrappers

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py](jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py)
- [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py](jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py)

</details>



This document covers the model wrapper system that enables integration of external neural network potentials into TorchANI-Amber. Model wrappers provide a standardized interface for different neural network architectures, handling coordinate transformations, neighbor list calculations, and unit conversions.

For information about the core C++ integration layer, see [C++ Engine and JIT System](#3.1). For simulation configuration details, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1).

## Purpose and Architecture

Model wrappers serve as adaptation layers that allow external neural network potentials to interface with the TorchANI-Amber system. They handle the differences in input formats, coordinate systems, and output structures between various neural network implementations.

### Wrapper System Architecture

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "External Models"
        AIMNET["AimNet2 Models<br/>.pt files"]
        NUTMEG["Nutmeg Models<br/>.pt files"]
        OTHER["Other NN Models"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Wrapper Layer"
        AIM_WRAP["AimNet2Wrapper<br/>torchani.nn.Module"]
        AIM_MBIS["AimNet2Mbis<br/>torchani.nn.Module"]
        NUT_WRAP["NutmegWrapper<br/>torchani.nn.Module"]
    end
    
    subgraph "TorchANI Interface"
        COMMON["Common Interface<br/>forward(species_coords)"]
        NLIST["Neighbor Lists<br/>AdaptiveList"]
        UNITS["Unit Conversion<br/>Hartree/eV/kJ·mol⁻¹"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        SPECIES["Species Tensors"]
        ENERGIES["Energy Values"]
        CHARGES["Atomic Charges"]
    end
    
    AIMNET --> AIM_WRAP
    AIMNET --> AIM_MBIS
    NUTMEG --> NUT_WRAP
    OTHER --> NUT_WRAP
    
    AIM_WRAP --> COMMON
    AIM_MBIS --> COMMON
    NUT_WRAP --> COMMON
    
    COMMON --> NLIST
    COMMON --> UNITS
    
    NLIST --> SPECIES
    UNITS --> ENERGIES
    COMMON --> CHARGES
    
    style AIM_WRAP fill:#e1f5fe
    style COMMON fill:#e8f5e8
    style NLIST fill:#fff3e0
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:54-338](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:18-152]()

### Data Flow Through Wrappers

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        COORDS["Coordinates<br/>Tensor[batch, atoms, 3]"]
        SPECIES["Species<br/>Tensor[batch, atoms]"]
        CELL["Cell Parameters<br/>Optional[Tensor]"]
        PBC["Periodic Boundary<br/>Optional[Tensor]"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Wrapper Processing"
        NLIST_CALC["Neighbor List<br/>AdaptiveList._nlist()"]
        COORD_TRANS["Coordinate Transform<br/>Units & Format"]
        FEAT_BUILD["Feature Building<br/>Atom Types & Charges"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Execution"
        EXTERNAL["External Model<br/>model.forward()"]
        POST_PROC["Post Processing<br/>Unit Conversion"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output"
        OUT_SPECIES["Species"]
        OUT_ENERGY["Energies"]
        OUT_CHARGES["Atomic Charges"]
    end
    
    COORDS --> NLIST_CALC
    SPECIES --> NLIST_CALC
    CELL --> NLIST_CALC
    PBC --> NLIST_CALC
    
    NLIST_CALC --> COORD_TRANS
    COORD_TRANS --> FEAT_BUILD
    FEAT_BUILD --> EXTERNAL
    
    EXTERNAL --> POST_PROC
    POST_PROC --> OUT_SPECIES
    POST_PROC --> OUT_ENERGY
    POST_PROC --> OUT_CHARGES
    
    style NLIST_CALC fill:#fff3e0
    style EXTERNAL fill:#e1f5fe
    style POST_PROC fill:#e8f5e8
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:120-195](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:106-151]()

## AimNet2 Wrapper System

The AimNet2 wrapper system provides integration for AimNet2 neural network potentials, supporting multiple long-range electrostatic treatment methods and charge prediction schemes.

### AimNet2Wrapper Class

The `AimNet2Wrapper` class provides the primary interface for AimNet2 models:

| Component | Description | Configuration |
|-----------|-------------|---------------|
| `method_lr` | Long-range method | `"simple"`, `"dsf"`, `"ewald"` |
| `cutoff_lr` | Long-range cutoff | `None` (auto), or float value |
| `dsf_alpha` | DSF damping parameter | `None` (auto), or float value |
| `output_hartree` | Energy units | `True` (Hartree), `False` (eV) |

**Core Methods:**

- `from_jit_file(path, device, **kwargs)` - Load model from JIT file
- `forward(species_coords, cell, pbc, charge, atomic, ensemble_values)` - Main inference
- `_calc_neighbors(species, coords, cell, pbc)` - Neighbor list calculation

### Long-Range Electrostatic Methods

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Method Types"
        SIMPLE["method_lr='simple'<br/>No cutoff (inf)"]
        DSF["method_lr='dsf'<br/>Damped Shifted Force"]
        EWALD["method_lr='ewald'<br/>Ewald summation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration"
        CUTOFF["cutoff_lr parameter<br/>Default: 15.0 Å"]
        ALPHA["dsf_alpha parameter<br/>Default: 0.2"]
        VALIDATION["Parameter Validation<br/>_validate_lr_params()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Application"
        MODULE_FIND["Find .lrcoulomb modules<br/>model.named_modules()"]
        METHOD_SET["Set module.method<br/>Set module.dsf_alpha"]
        CUTOFF_CHECK["Validate cutoff_lr < model.cutoff"]
    end
    
    SIMPLE --> CUTOFF
    DSF --> CUTOFF
    DSF --> ALPHA
    EWALD --> CUTOFF
    
    CUTOFF --> VALIDATION
    ALPHA --> VALIDATION
    VALIDATION --> MODULE_FIND
    
    MODULE_FIND --> METHOD_SET
    METHOD_SET --> CUTOFF_CHECK
    
    style DSF fill:#e1f5fe
    style VALIDATION fill:#fff3e0
    style METHOD_SET fill:#e8f5e8
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:74-95](), [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:100-104]()

### AimNet2Mbis Charge Prediction

The `AimNet2Mbis` class extends `AimNet2Wrapper` to use MBIS (Minimal Basis Iterative Stockholder) charge prediction instead of Hirshfeld charges:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "AimNet2Mbis Components"
        BASE["AimNet2Wrapper<br/>Base functionality"]
        ASSEMBLER["Assembler<br/>ANIq model builder"]
        CHARGE_NET["Charge Networks<br/>_ANINetworksDiscardFirstScalar"]
        NORMALIZER["ChargeNormalizer<br/>electronegativity_and_hardness"]
    end
    
    subgraph "State Dict Loading"
        ANI2X["ani2x_state_dict.pt<br/>AEV parameters"]
        CHARGE_DICT["charge_nn_state_dict.pt<br/>Charge network weights"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Flow"
        AIMNET_FORWARD["_run_aimnet_forward()<br/>Energy calculation"]
        CHARGE_FORWARD["_charge_model.compute_from_neighbors()<br/>MBIS charges"]
        COMBINE["Combine results<br/>SpeciesEnergiesAtomicCharges"]
    end
    
    BASE --> ASSEMBLER
    ASSEMBLER --> CHARGE_NET
    CHARGE_NET --> NORMALIZER
    
    ANI2X --> CHARGE_NET
    CHARGE_DICT --> CHARGE_NET
    
    AIMNET_FORWARD --> CHARGE_FORWARD
    CHARGE_FORWARD --> COMBINE
    
    style CHARGE_NET fill:#e1f5fe
    style COMBINE fill:#e8f5e8
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:257-338](), [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:268-298]()

## Nutmeg Wrapper System

The `NutmegWrapper` class provides integration for Nutmeg neural network potentials, which use different atomic representations and units.

### Atomic Number Mapping

Nutmeg models use a specific mapping from atomic numbers to internal indices:

| Atomic Number | Element | Internal Index |
|---------------|---------|----------------|
| 1 | H | 0 |
| 6 | C | 3 |
| 7 | N | 4 |
| 8 | O | 5 |
| 9 | F | 6 |
| 16 | S | 11 |
| 17 | Cl | 12 |
| 35 | Br | 15 |
| 53 | I | 16 |

### Feature Engineering

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Input Processing"
        SPECIES_IN["Species Tensor<br/>Atomic numbers"]
        COORDS_IN["Coordinates<br/>Angstroms"]
        CHARGES_IN["Atomic Charges<br/>Gasteiger charges"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Feature Creation"
        TYPE_MAP["_types_map<br/>Z_NUM_IDX_MAP lookup"]
        ONE_HOT["One-hot encoding<br/>17 element types"]
        CHARGE_FEAT["Charge features<br/>_atomic_charges"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model Input"
        NODE_ATTRS["node_attrs<br/>Concatenated features"]
        EDGE_INDEX["edge_index<br/>Neighbor pairs"]
        COORDINATES["coordinates<br/>Nanometers"]
        CELL_SHIFT["cell_shift_vector<br/>PBC shifts"]
    end
    
    SPECIES_IN --> TYPE_MAP
    TYPE_MAP --> ONE_HOT
    CHARGES_IN --> CHARGE_FEAT
    
    ONE_HOT --> NODE_ATTRS
    CHARGE_FEAT --> NODE_ATTRS
    COORDS_IN --> COORDINATES
    
    NODE_ATTRS --> MODEL_INPUT["Nutmeg Model"]
    EDGE_INDEX --> MODEL_INPUT
    COORDINATES --> MODEL_INPUT
    CELL_SHIFT --> MODEL_INPUT
    
    style TYPE_MAP fill:#fff3e0
    style NODE_ATTRS fill:#e1f5fe
    style MODEL_INPUT fill:#e8f5e8
```

**Sources:** [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:19-37](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:70-81](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:134-149]()

### Unit Conversion System

The Nutmeg wrapper handles multiple unit conversions:

| Conversion | Factor | Purpose |
|------------|--------|---------|
| kJ/mol → Hartree | `1 / HARTREE_TO_KJOULEMOL` | Energy units |
| Angstrom → Nanometer | `0.1` | Distance units |
| Cutoff scaling | `/self._angstrom_to_nm` | Neighbor list cutoff |

**Sources:** [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:54-56]()

## Common Interface Patterns

All model wrappers implement a consistent interface for integration with the TorchANI-Amber system.

### Standard Forward Method Signature

```python
def forward(
    self,
    species_coords: Tuple[Tensor, Tensor],
    cell: Optional[Tensor] = None,
    pbc: Optional[Tensor] = None,
    charge: int = 0,
    atomic: bool = False,
    ensemble_values: bool = False,
    _molecule_idxs: Optional[Tensor] = None,
) -> Union[SpeciesEnergiesAtomicCharges, Tuple[Tensor, Tensor]]
```

### Neighbor List Management

All wrappers use the `AdaptiveList` neighbor list implementation:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Neighbor List Workflow"
        INIT["AdaptiveList()<br/>Initialize neighbor list"]
        COMPUTE["_nlist(cutoff, species, coords, cell, pbc)<br/>Compute neighbors"]
        FILTER["discard_inter_molecule_pairs()<br/>Optional molecule filtering"]
        PROCESS["Wrapper-specific processing<br/>Format conversion"]
    end
    
    INIT --> COMPUTE
    COMPUTE --> FILTER
    FILTER --> PROCESS
    
    style COMPUTE fill:#e1f5fe
    style FILTER fill:#fff3e0
    style PROCESS fill:#e8f5e8
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:99](), [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:232-254](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:60](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:82-104]()

### JIT Compilation Support

Model wrappers support TorchScript compilation for deployment:

```python
# Example compilation pattern
model = AimNet2Wrapper.from_jit_file("model.pt")
scripted_model = torch.jit.script(model)
torch.jit.save(scripted_model, "compiled_model.pt")
```

**Sources:** [jit/aimnet2_wrapper.py:481-487](), [jit/nutmeg_wrapper.py:156-159]()
