# Page: Amber Integration

# Amber Integration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [ani-amber-logo-dark.png](ani-amber-logo-dark.png)
- [ani-amber-logo-light.png](ani-amber-logo-light.png)
- [src/electro.cpp](src/electro.cpp)
- [src/electro.h](src/electro.h)
- [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja](tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja)
- [tests/test_amber_integration.py](tests/test_amber_integration.py)

</details>



This document provides a comprehensive overview of how TorchANI integrates with the Amber molecular dynamics simulation suite. It covers the architecture, integration modes, and configuration mechanisms that enable neural network potentials to be used within Amber's `pmemd` and `sander` engines.

For detailed configuration options and namelist parameters, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For ML/MM setup specifics and coupling schemes, see [ML/MM Setup and Coupling](#4.2). For example configurations and templates, see [Input Templates and Examples](#4.3).

## Integration Architecture

TorchANI-Amber provides two primary integration pathways with Amber: external potential interface for full-ML simulations and QM/MM interface for hybrid ML/MM simulations. Both pathways utilize the same core C++ engine but interface with different Amber subsystems.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Amber MD Engines"
        PMEMD["pmemd"]
        SANDER["sander"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Interfaces"
        EXTPOT["External Potential Interface<br/>iextpot=1, extprog='TORCHANI'"]
        QMMM["QM/MM Interface<br/>ifqnt=1, qm_theory='EXTERN'"]
    end
    
    subgraph "TorchANI Core Engine"
        CAPI["torchani.h<br/>C API Functions"]
        FAPI["torchani.F90<br/>Fortran Interface"]
        CPP["torchani.cpp<br/>Core Implementation"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Neural Network Backend"
        JIT["PyTorch JIT Models<br/>.pt files"]
        CUAEV["cuAEV Extensions<br/>CUDA Acceleration"]
    end
    
    PMEMD --> EXTPOT
    PMEMD --> QMMM
    SANDER --> EXTPOT
    SANDER --> QMMM
    
    EXTPOT --> FAPI
    QMMM --> FAPI
    FAPI --> CAPI
    CAPI --> CPP
    
    CPP --> JIT
    CPP --> CUAEV
```

Sources: [README.md:9-18](), [README.md:172-184](), [tests/test_amber_integration.py:32-76]()

## Integration Modes

TorchANI-Amber supports two distinct integration modes, each targeting different simulation scenarios and utilizing different Amber interfaces.

### Full-ML Mode

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Amber Configuration"
        MDIN1["mdin file<br/>iextpot=1"]
        EXTPOT1["&extpot namelist<br/>extprog='TORCHANI'"]
        ANI1["&ani namelist<br/>model configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Flow"
        AMBER1["Amber Engine"] --> EXT_IF["External Potential<br/>Interface"]
        EXT_IF --> TORCHANI1["TorchANI Engine"]
        TORCHANI1 --> FORCES1["Forces & Energies"]
        FORCES1 --> AMBER1
    end
    
    MDIN1 --> AMBER1
    EXTPOT1 --> EXT_IF
    ANI1 --> TORCHANI1
```

In full-ML mode, the entire molecular system's potential energy is calculated using neural network models. This mode uses Amber's external potential interface (`iextpot=1`) and requires the `&extpot` namelist with `extprog='TORCHANI'`.

### ML/MM Mode

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Amber Configuration"
        MDIN2["mdin file<br/>ifqnt=1"]
        QMMM2["&qmmm namelist<br/>qm_theory='EXTERN'"]
        ANI2["&ani namelist<br/>ML/MM options"]
    end
    
    subgraph "System Partitioning"
        QM_REGION["QM Region<br/>(Neural Network)"]
        MM_REGION["MM Region<br/>(Force Field)"]
        COUPLING["ML/MM Coupling<br/>Electrostatic"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Integration Flow"
        AMBER2["Sander Engine"] --> QMMM_IF["QM/MM Interface"]
        QMMM_IF --> QM_REGION
        QMMM_IF --> MM_REGION
        QM_REGION --> COUPLING
        MM_REGION --> COUPLING
        COUPLING --> FORCES2["Combined Forces"]
        FORCES2 --> AMBER2
    end
    
    MDIN2 --> AMBER2
    QMMM2 --> QMMM_IF
    ANI2 --> QM_REGION
```

ML/MM mode partitions the system into QM and MM regions, using neural networks for the QM region and classical force fields for the MM region. This mode requires `ifqnt=1` and uses Amber's QM/MM subsystem with `qm_theory='EXTERN'`.

Sources: [README.md:116-170](), [README.md:172-257](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:3-47]()

## Electrostatic Coupling Mechanisms

The ML/MM interface implements sophisticated electrostatic coupling schemes to handle the interaction between QM and MM regions.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Coupling Types"
        COULOMBIC["Coulombic Coupling<br/>mlmm_coupling=0<br/>Fixed charges"]
        POLARIZABLE["Simple Polarizable Coupling<br/>mlmm_coupling=1<br/>Variable charges"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Charge Handling"
        FIXED["use_torchani_charges=false<br/>Topology charges"]
        PREDICTED["use_torchani_charges=true<br/>Neural network charges"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Electrostatic Functions"
        COULOMB_FUNC["coulombic_embedding_energy()<br/>electro.cpp:78-88"]
        POLAR_FUNC["polarizable_embedding_energy()<br/>electro.cpp:61-77"]
        EFIELD["calc_efield()<br/>electro.cpp:24-39"]
    end
    
    COULOMBIC --> FIXED
    COULOMBIC --> COULOMB_FUNC
    POLARIZABLE --> PREDICTED
    POLARIZABLE --> POLAR_FUNC
    POLAR_FUNC --> EFIELD
```

The electrostatic coupling is implemented through dedicated functions in the `electro` namespace that calculate electric fields, polarization energies, and Coulombic interactions between QM and MM regions.

Sources: [src/electro.cpp:78-88](), [src/electro.cpp:61-77](), [src/electro.h:4-18](), [README.md:197-212]()

## Configuration Flow

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Input Configuration"
        TEMPLATE["Jinja2 Templates<br/>input.mdin.jinja"]
        MDIN["Generated mdin file"]
        SYSTEM["System Files<br/>.prmtop, .inpcrd"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Runtime Configuration"
        NAMELISTS["Amber Namelists<br/>&cntrl, &extpot, &qmmm, &ani"]
        INIT["torchani_initialize()"]
        MODEL_LOAD["Model Loading<br/>torch::jit::load()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Flow"
        MD_LOOP["MD Time Step"]
        COORD_PASS["Coordinate Transfer"]
        ENERGY_CALC["Energy/Force Calculation"]
        FORCE_RETURN["Force Return"]
    end
    
    TEMPLATE --> MDIN
    MDIN --> NAMELISTS
    NAMELISTS --> INIT
    INIT --> MODEL_LOAD
    MODEL_LOAD --> MD_LOOP
    
    MD_LOOP --> COORD_PASS
    COORD_PASS --> ENERGY_CALC
    ENERGY_CALC --> FORCE_RETURN
    FORCE_RETURN --> MD_LOOP
```

The configuration process involves template-based mdin file generation, namelist parsing, model initialization, and runtime execution through Amber's MD loop.

Sources: [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:1-98](), [tests/test_amber_integration.py:344-380]()

## Interface API Structure

The integration is implemented through a layered API structure that provides both C and Fortran interfaces to accommodate Amber's mixed-language codebase.

| Interface Layer | File | Purpose |
|----------------|------|---------|
| Fortran Interface | `torchani.F90` | Amber-compatible Fortran bindings |
| C API | `torchani.h` | C function declarations and types |
| Core Implementation | `torchani.cpp` | PyTorch JIT model execution |
| Electrostatic Coupling | `electro.cpp` | ML/MM interaction calculations |

The API supports both full-ML calculations where TorchANI handles the entire system potential and ML/MM calculations where it integrates with Amber's QM/MM infrastructure.

## Configuration Namelist Overview

TorchANI-Amber uses Amber's namelist system for configuration, with different namelists required for different integration modes:

| Namelist | Required For | Key Parameters |
|----------|-------------|----------------|
| `&cntrl` | All modes | `iextpot=1` (full-ML) or `ifqnt=1` (ML/MM) |
| `&extpot` | Full-ML only | `extprog='TORCHANI'` |
| `&qmmm` | ML/MM only | `qm_theory='EXTERN'`, `qmmask` |
| `&ani` | All modes | `model_type`, `use_cuda_device`, coupling options |

The `&ani` namelist contains TorchANI-specific options including model selection, precision settings, CUDA configuration, and ML/MM coupling parameters.

Sources: [README.md:123-151](), [README.md:180-207](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:48-96]()

# Page: Simulation Configuration

# Simulation Configuration

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [ani-amber-logo-dark.png](ani-amber-logo-dark.png)
- [ani-amber-logo-light.png](ani-amber-logo-light.png)
- [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja](benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja)
- [run-cmake](run-cmake)

</details>



This page covers how to configure molecular dynamics simulations with TorchANI-Amber through `mdin` input files. It explains the required namelists, configuration options, and provides examples for both full-ML and ML/MM simulation types.

For information about ML/MM coupling mechanisms and charge prediction methods, see [ML/MM Setup and Coupling](#4.2). For ready-to-use configuration templates, see [Input Templates and Examples](#4.3).

## Configuration Overview

TorchANI-Amber integrates with Amber through specific namelist configurations in `mdin` files. The configuration approach depends on the simulation type:

### Configuration Types

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Simulation Configuration"
        A["mdin Input File"] --> B{"Simulation Type"}
        
        B --> C["Full-ML Simulation"]
        B --> D["ML/MM Simulation"]
        
        C --> E["&cntrl namelist<br/>iextpot = 1"]
        C --> F["&extpot namelist<br/>extprog = 'TORCHANI'"]
        C --> G["&ani namelist<br/>TorchANI configuration"]
        
        D --> H["&cntrl namelist<br/>ifqnt = 1"]
        D --> I["&qmmm namelist<br/>qm_theory = 'EXTERN'"]
        D --> J["&ani namelist<br/>TorchANI + ML/MM configuration"]
        
        E --> K["Complete mdin"]
        F --> K
        G --> K
        H --> L["Complete mdin"]
        I --> L
        J --> L
    end
```

Sources: [README.md:116-122](), [README.md:172-183]()

## Full-ML Configuration

Full-ML simulations use neural network potentials for the entire molecular system. This requires three specific namelists:

### Required Namelists Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Full-ML mdin Structure"
        A["&cntrl"] --> B["Standard Amber options<br/>+ iextpot = 1"]
        C["&extpot"] --> D["extprog = 'TORCHANI'"]
        E["&ani"] --> F["Neural network<br/>configuration"]
        
        B --> G["Complete Configuration"]
        D --> G
        F --> G
    end
```

### Core Configuration Options

The `&ani` namelist contains the primary TorchANI configuration:

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `model_type` | string | `"ani1x"` | Neural network model (`"ani1x"`, `"ani1ccx"`, `"ani2x"`, `"anidr"`) |
| `use_double_precision` | bool | `.true.` | Use float64 parameters for accurate dynamics |
| `use_cuda_device` | bool | `.true.` | Enable GPU acceleration |
| `use_cuaev` | bool | - | Use cuAEV CUDA extension for supported models |
| `use_amber_neighborlist` | bool | - | Use Amber's neighborlist calculation |
| `model_index` | int | `-1` | Select specific model from ensemble (-1 = use full ensemble) |
| `cuda_device_index` | int | `0` | GPU device index |

Sources: [README.md:123-151]()

### Example Full-ML Configuration

```fortran
&cntrl
    iextpot = 1 ! Required to run full-ML TorchANI-Amber
    ! ... Add the rest of the Sander options here
/
&extpot
    extprog = "TORCHANI"  ! Required to run full-ML TorchANI-Amber
/
&ani
    model_type = "ani2x"
    use_double_precision = .true.
    use_cuda_device = .true.
    use_cuaev = .true.
    ! ... Add the rest of the TorchANI-Amber config options here
/
```

Sources: [README.md:152-169]()

## ML/MM Configuration

ML/MM simulations partition the system into QM (quantum mechanical) and MM (molecular mechanical) regions, with the QM region handled by neural networks.

### ML/MM Namelist Structure

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ML/MM mdin Structure"
        A["&cntrl"] --> B["Standard Amber options<br/>+ ifqnt = 1"]
        C["&qmmm"] --> D["qm_theory = 'EXTERN'<br/>qm_ewald = 0<br/>qmmm_int = 1"]
        E["&ani"] --> F["Neural network +<br/>ML/MM configuration"]
        
        B --> G["Complete Configuration"]
        D --> G
        F --> G
    end
```

### Required QM/MM Parameters

The `&qmmm` namelist requires specific settings:

| Parameter | Value | Purpose |
|-----------|-------|---------|
| `qm_theory` | `'EXTERN'` | Use external program (TorchANI) for QM region |
| `qm_ewald` | `0` | Required for Sander EXTERN QM/MM |
| `qmmm_int` | `1` | Let TorchANI-Amber handle ML/MM coupling |
| `qmmask` | Selection string | Define QM region (e.g., `':1'` for first molecule) |
| `qmcut` | Distance | Recommended: `15.0` Å |

Sources: [README.md:181-183](), [README.md:223-228]()

### ML/MM Specific Options

The `&ani` namelist includes additional ML/MM configuration:

#### Output Control
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `write_xyz` | bool | Dump QM region coordinates to `.xyz` file |
| `write_forces` | bool | Dump QM atom forces to `.dat` file |
| `write_charges` | bool | Dump QM atom charges to `.dat` file |
| `write_charges_grad` | bool | Dump charge derivatives to `.dat` file |

#### Coupling Configuration
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `use_torchani_charges` | bool | Use NN-predicted charges (requires charge-predicting model) |
| `mlmm_coupling` | int | Coupling type: `0` (coulombic), `1` (simple polarizable) |

Sources: [README.md:187-207]()

### Recommended ML/MM Configurations

#### Configuration 1: Variable NN-Predicted Charges
```fortran
&cntrl
    ifqnt = 1  ! Required for all ML/MM TorchANI-Amber dynamics
    ! ... Add extra simulation settings here
/
&qmmm
    qm_theory = 'EXTERN'  ! Required for all ML/MM TorchANI-Amber dynamics
    qm_ewald = 0  ! Required for Sander EXTERN QM/MM
    qmmm_int = 1  ! Required, let TorchANI-Amber handle the ML/MM coupling
    qmmask = ':1',  ! Select the first molecule as the QM-region
    qmcut = 15.0  ! Recommended
/
&ani
    model_type = 'animbis'  ! Charge-predicting model
    use_torchani_charges = .true.  ! Use geometry dependent, nn-predicted charges
    mlmm_coupling = 1  ! Simple polarizable coupling
/
```

#### Configuration 2: Fixed Topology Charges
```fortran
&cntrl
    ifqnt = 1  ! Required for all ML/MM TorchANI-Amber dynamics
    ! ... Add extra simulation settings here
/
&qmmm
    qm_theory = 'EXTERN'  ! Required for all ML/MM TorchANI-Amber dynamics
    qm_ewald = 0  ! Required for Sander EXTERN QM/MM
    qmmm_int = 1  ! Required, let TorchANI-Amber handle the ML/MM coupling
    qmmask = ':1'  ! Select the first molecule as the QM-region
    qmcut = 15.0  ! Recommended
/
&ani
    model_type = 'ani2x'  ! Select any model
    use_torchani_charges = .false.  ! Use fixed topology charges
    mlmm_coupling = 0  ! Coulombic coupling
/
```

Sources: [README.md:215-257]()

## Configuration Templates

TorchANI-Amber provides Jinja2 templates for automated configuration generation, particularly useful for benchmarking and systematic studies.

### Template Structure

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph "Template System"
        A["mlmm.mdin.jinja"] --> B["Jinja2 Template Engine"]
        C["Configuration Parameters"] --> B
        B --> D["Generated mdin File"]
        
        E["Template Variables"] --> F["mlmm.protocol"]
        E --> G["mlmm.selection"]
        E --> H["mlmm.cutoff"]
        E --> I["mlmm.cuda"]
        E --> J["mlmm.float64"]
        
        F --> K["ani_me<br/>ani_mbispol<br/>sander_me"]
        G --> L["QM region mask"]
        H --> M["QM/MM cutoff"]
        I --> N["GPU usage"]
        J --> O["Precision level"]
    end
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:1-88]()

### Template Parameters

The ML/MM template accepts these key parameters:

| Parameter | Values | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| `mlmm.protocol` | `"ani_me"`, `"ani_mbispol"`, `"sander_me"` | ML/MM coupling protocol |
| `mlmm.selection` | Amber mask | QM region selection |
| `mlmm.cutoff` | Float | QM/MM interaction cutoff |
| `mlmm.cuda` | Boolean | Enable CUDA acceleration |
| `mlmm.float64` | Boolean | Use double precision |
| `dump_traj` | Boolean | Control output verbosity |

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:36-84]()

### Protocol-Specific Configuration

The template automatically configures different ML/MM protocols:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "Protocol Configuration Logic"
        A["mlmm.protocol"] --> B{"Protocol Type"}
        
        B --> C["ani_me"]
        B --> D["ani_mbispol"] 
        B --> E["sander_me"]
        
        C --> F["model_type = 'ani2x'<br/>mlmm_coupling = 0<br/>use_torchani_charges = .False."]
        D --> G["model_type = 'animbis'<br/>mlmm_coupling = 1<br/>use_torchani_charges = .True."]
        E --> H["model_type = 'ani2x'<br/>qmmm_int = 5<br/>allow_untested_protocols = .True."]
    end
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:39-70]()

## Advanced Configuration Options

For experimental features and advanced use cases, additional options are available:

### Experimental Features

| Feature | Parameters | Description |
|---------|------------|-------------|
| Switching | `use_switching_function`, `switching_program`, `qlow`, `qhigh` | Mix NN potential with external QM program |
| ExtCoupling | `use_extcoupling`, `extcoupling_program` | Use external program for QM/MM interaction |
| Numerical Forces | `use_numerical_qmmm_forces` | Calculate ML/MM coupling numerically |

### Element-Specific Polarizabilities

Fixed atomic polarizabilities can be specified using `pol_<element>` format:
- `pol_H`, `pol_C`, `pol_N`, `pol_O`, etc. (up to `Ne`)

Sources: [README.md:376-421]()

# Page: ML/MM Setup and Coupling

# ML/MM Setup and Coupling

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [README.md](README.md)
- [ani-amber-logo-dark.png](ani-amber-logo-dark.png)
- [ani-amber-logo-light.png](ani-amber-logo-light.png)
- [src/electro.cpp](src/electro.cpp)
- [src/electro.h](src/electro.h)
- [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja](tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja)
- [tests/test_amber_integration.py](tests/test_amber_integration.py)

</details>



This document covers the setup and configuration of quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) simulations using TorchANI-Amber, where a portion of the system is treated with neural network potentials (QM region) while the remainder uses classical force fields (MM region). For information about full-ML simulations where the entire system uses neural networks, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For implementation details of the core C++ engine, see [C++ Engine and JIT System](#3.1).

## Overview

ML/MM simulations in TorchANI-Amber partition the molecular system into two regions: a QM region calculated using neural network potentials and an MM region using classical Amber force fields. The interface handles the electrostatic and van der Waals interactions between these regions through various coupling schemes.

## Configuration Requirements

### Basic Namelist Setup

ML/MM simulations require three key namelists in the `mdin` input file:

**Control Namelist (`&cntrl`)**
- `ifqnt = 1` - Enables QM/MM functionality
- Standard MD parameters (timestep, temperature, etc.)

**QM/MM Namelist (`&qmmm`)**
- `qm_theory = 'EXTERN'` - Specifies external QM program (TorchANI)
- `qm_ewald = 0` - Required for external QM/MM
- `qmmm_int = 1` - Default, lets TorchANI handle ML/MM coupling
- `qmmask = ':1'` - Defines QM region atoms
- `qmcut = 15.0` - QM/MM interaction cutoff distance

**ANI Namelist (`&ani`)**
- Standard TorchANI parameters plus ML/MM specific options

Sources: [README.md:172-183](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:36-42]()

### ML/MM Configuration Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["mdin Input File"] --> B["&cntrl namelist"]
    A --> C["&qmmm namelist"] 
    A --> D["&ani namelist"]
    
    B --> E["ifqnt = 1"]
    C --> F["qm_theory = 'EXTERN'"]
    C --> G["qm_ewald = 0"]
    C --> H["qmmm_int = 1"]
    C --> I["qmmask definition"]
    
    D --> J["mlmm_coupling"]
    D --> K["use_torchani_charges"]
    D --> L["Standard ANI options"]
    
    E --> M["Amber QM/MM Engine"]
    F --> M
    G --> M
    H --> M
    I --> M
    
    J --> N["Coupling Method Selection"]
    K --> O["Charge Handling"]
    
    M --> P["TorchANI ML/MM Interface"]
    N --> P
    O --> P
```

Sources: [README.md:177-183](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:3-47]()

## Coupling Schemes

TorchANI-Amber supports two primary coupling methods controlled by the `mlmm_coupling` parameter:

### Coulombic Coupling (mlmm_coupling = 0)

This represents mechanical embedding where QM and MM regions interact through fixed point charges:

- Uses topology-defined charges from the parameter file
- QM region charges remain constant during simulation
- Simpler implementation, faster computation
- Recommended with `use_torchani_charges = .false.`

### Simple Polarizable Coupling (mlmm_coupling = 1)

This advanced method includes polarization effects:

- Supports geometry-dependent charge prediction
- Includes distortion energy corrections
- More accurate for systems with significant charge transfer
- Recommended with `use_torchani_charges = .true.` and charge-predicting models

Sources: [README.md:205-212](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:66-84]()

### Coupling Implementation Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["QM Region"] --> B["torchani_calculate_forces"]
    C["MM Region"] --> D["Amber Force Field"]
    
    B --> E["QM Energies & Forces"]
    D --> F["MM Energies & Forces"]
    
    E --> G["electro::coulombic_embedding_energy"]
    F --> G
    C --> H["MM Point Charges"]
    H --> G
    
    E --> I["electro::polarizable_embedding_energy"]
    F --> I
    J["Atomic Polarizabilities"] --> I
    
    G --> K["Total QM/MM Energy"]
    I --> K
    K --> L["Combined System Forces"]
```

Sources: [src/electro.h:4-18](), [src/electro.cpp:78-89]()

## Charge Prediction and Handling

### Geometry-Dependent Charges

When `use_torchani_charges = .true.`, the system uses neural network-predicted charges:

- Currently supported by `animbis` model type
- Charges predicted at each MD step based on geometry
- Charge derivatives contribute to forces via `use_charges_derivatives`
- MBIS atomic charges at wB97X/def2-TZVPP level for ANI-mbis

### Fixed Topology Charges

When `use_torchani_charges = .false.`:

- Uses charges from Amber topology file
- Charges remain constant throughout simulation
- Faster computation, suitable for mechanical embedding

Sources: [README.md:198-204](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:67-77]()

### Charge Handling Implementation

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["use_torchani_charges"] --> B{".true. or .false."}
    
    B -->|".true."| C["Neural Network Charge Prediction"]
    B -->|".false."| D["Topology File Charges"]
    
    C --> E["Model Forward Pass"]
    E --> F["Geometry-Dependent Charges"]
    F --> G["Charge Derivatives Calculation"]
    
    D --> H["Fixed Point Charges"]
    
    G --> I["electro::coulombic_embedding_energy"]
    H --> I
    
    I --> J["QM/MM Electrostatic Energy"]
    J --> K["Force Contribution"]
```

Sources: [README.md:201-204](), [tests/test_amber_integration.py:33-36]()

## Recommended Configurations

The system provides two main recommended setups:

### Configuration 1: Variable Neural Network Charges
```
mlmm_coupling = 1
use_torchani_charges = .true.
model_type = "animbis"
```

### Configuration 2: Fixed Topology Charges  
```
mlmm_coupling = 0
use_torchani_charges = .false.
model_type = "ani2x"  # or any standard model
```

Sources: [README.md:209-212]()

## Advanced Options

### Experimental Features

**Switching Function (`use_switching_function`)**
- Dynamically switches between neural network and external QM methods
- Based on prediction uncertainty between ensemble models
- Controlled by `qlow` and `qhigh` parameters

**External Coupling (`use_extcoupling`)**
- Uses external QM program for QM/MM interactions
- Supports DFTB, ORCA, and LIO programs
- Specified via `extcoupling_program`

**Alternative QM/MM Integration (`qmmm_int = 5`)**
- Lets Amber handle MM/ML coupling directly
- May provide better PBC handling
- Always uses force field charges regardless of `&ani` settings

Sources: [README.md:356-421]()

### Output Control Options

The interface provides several debugging and analysis outputs:

| Option | Purpose | Output Format |
|--------|---------|---------------|
| `write_xyz` | QM region coordinates | `.xyz` file |
| `write_forces` | Forces on QM atoms | `.dat` file |
| `write_charges` | QM atomic charges | `.dat` file |
| `write_charges_grad` | Charge derivatives | `.dat` file |

Sources: [README.md:187-196](), [tests/templates/input.mdin.jinja:85-90]()

## Implementation Details

### Core Electrostatic Functions

The ML/MM coupling is implemented through two main functions in the `electro` namespace:

**`coulombic_embedding_energy`** - Calculates simple Coulombic interactions between QM and MM charges
**`polarizable_embedding_energy`** - Computes polarization energy including electric field effects and atomic polarizabilities

Both functions handle unit conversions between Amber (Angstrom/elementary charge) and atomic units (Bohr/Hartree).

Sources: [src/electro.h:13-17](), [src/electro.cpp:78-89]()

### Testing Framework

The ML/MM functionality is extensively tested with multiple configurations:

- Different coupling protocols (`me`, `mbispol`) 
- CUDA vs CPU execution
- Various precision levels (float32/float64)
- Shake constraints on/off
- Vacuum vs explicit solvent

Sources: [tests/test_amber_integration.py:80-86](), [tests/test_amber_integration.py:33-36]()

# Page: Input Templates and Examples

# Input Templates and Examples

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja](benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja)
- [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja](benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja)
- [run-cmake](run-cmake)

</details>



This page documents the Jinja2 template system used to generate Amber `mdin` input files for TorchANI-Amber simulations. The template system provides parameterized configurations for different simulation types, including full-ML simulations and ML/MM hybrid approaches.

For detailed information about simulation configuration parameters, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For ML/MM setup procedures, see [ML/MM Setup and Coupling](#4.2). For benchmarking workflows that use these templates, see [Bench CLI Tool](#5.1).

## Template System Architecture

The TorchANI-Amber system uses Jinja2 templates to generate standardized `mdin` input files for different simulation scenarios. This templating approach ensures consistent configuration while allowing parameterization for various system sizes, simulation protocols, and hardware configurations.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Template Files"
        MLMM["mlmm.mdin.jinja<br/>ML/MM Simulations"]
        SCALE["scaling.mdin.jinja<br/>Performance Testing"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Configuration Parameters"
        VARS["Template Variables<br/>tstep_num, model, cuda, etc."]
        PROTO["Protocol Settings<br/>ani_me, ani_mbispol, sander_me"]
        SYS["System Settings<br/>cutoff, shake, precision"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Generated Output"
        MDIN1["simulation.mdin<br/>ML/MM Configuration"]
        MDIN2["benchmark.mdin<br/>Scaling Configuration"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Amber Integration"
        AMBER["Amber MD Engine<br/>pmemd/sander"]
        SIM["Molecular Dynamics<br/>Simulation"]
    end
    
    MLMM --> MDIN1
    SCALE --> MDIN2
    
    VARS --> MLMM
    VARS --> SCALE
    PROTO --> MLMM
    SYS --> SCALE
    
    MDIN1 --> AMBER
    MDIN2 --> AMBER
    AMBER --> SIM
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja]()

## Template Types and Use Cases

TorchANI-Amber provides specialized templates for different simulation workflows. Each template is optimized for specific use cases and contains appropriate namelist configurations.

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ML/MM Template"
        MLMM_T["mlmm.mdin.jinja"]
        MLMM_T --> QM["QM Region<br/>TorchANI Potential"]
        MLMM_T --> MM["MM Region<br/>Amber Force Field"]
        MLMM_T --> COUP["Coupling Protocol<br/>ani_me, ani_mbispol, sander_me"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Scaling Template"
        SCALE_T["scaling.mdin.jinja"]
        SCALE_T --> FULL["Full-ML System<br/>iextpot=2"]
        SCALE_T --> PERF["Performance Testing<br/>Various System Sizes"]
        SCALE_T --> BENCH["Benchmarking<br/>cuAEV Toggle"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Common Features"
        THERMO["Thermostat Settings<br/>ntt=3, temp0=300.0"]
        SHAKE_OPT["SHAKE Options<br/>ntc, ntf, dt"]
        OUTPUT["Output Control<br/>ntwx, ntpr, ioutfm"]
    end
    
    QM --> THERMO
    MM --> THERMO
    FULL --> THERMO
    PERF --> SHAKE_OPT
    BENCH --> OUTPUT
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:1-88](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:1-49]()

## ML/MM Template Configuration

The `mlmm.mdin.jinja` template supports QM/MM simulations with TorchANI handling the quantum mechanical region. The template includes conditional logic for different coupling protocols and charge prediction methods.

### Core ML/MM Settings

| Parameter | Template Variable | Default | Description |
|-----------|------------------|---------|-------------|
| QM/MM Enable | `mlmm` | - | Boolean flag to enable QM/MM |
| QM Selection | `mlmm.selection` | - | Atom mask for QM region |
| QM Cutoff | `mlmm.cutoff` | - | QM-MM interaction cutoff |
| Coupling Protocol | `mlmm.protocol` | - | `ani_me`, `ani_mbispol`, `sander_me` |

### Protocol-Specific Configuration

The template uses conditional blocks to configure different ML/MM coupling approaches:

**ANI Mechanical Embedding (`ani_me`)**:
- `qmmm_int = 1` (ANI-controlled coupling)
- `mlmm_coupling = 0` 
- `use_torchani_charges = .False.`
- `model_type = "ani2x"`

**ANI Multi-Body Interaction Scheme Polarization (`ani_mbispol`)**:
- `qmmm_int = 1` (ANI-controlled coupling)
- `mlmm_coupling = 1`
- `use_torchani_charges = .True.`
- `model_type = "animbis"`

**Sander Mechanical Embedding (`sander_me`)**:
- `qmmm_int = 5` (Sander-controlled coupling)
- `mlmm_coupling = 0`
- `use_torchani_charges = .False.`
- `allow_untested_protocols = .True.`

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:28-46](), [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:47-85]()

### Output Control Variables

The template includes conditional output settings based on the `dump_traj` variable:

```
{% if dump_traj %}
ntwx = 1
ntpr = 1
write_charges = .True.
write_forces = .True.
write_xyz = .True.
{% else %}
ntwx = {{ tstep_num }}
ntpr = {{ tstep_num }}
write_charges = .False.
{% endif %}
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:21-27](), [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:74-84]()

## Scaling Template Configuration

The `scaling.mdin.jinja` template is designed for performance benchmarking and scaling studies. It configures full-ML simulations where the entire system uses TorchANI potentials via the external potential interface.

### External Potential Setup

The template configures TorchANI as an external potential using:

```
iextpot = 2  ! Use ANI as an external potential
extprog = "torchani"  ! Use ANI as an external potential
```

### Performance-Related Parameters

| Parameter | Template Variable | Options | Description |
|-----------|------------------|---------|-------------|
| GPU Usage | `cuda` | `True`/`False` | Enable CUDA acceleration |
| cuAEV Extension | `cuaev` | `True`/`False` | Use optimized CUDA AEV |
| Model Type | `model` | `ani1x`, `ani2x`, etc. | Neural network model |
| Neighborlist | `use_amber_neighborlist` | `True`/`False` | Use Amber neighborlist |
| Precision | - | `False` (float32) | Use single precision |

### SHAKE Configuration

The template includes conditional SHAKE settings:

```
{% if shake %}
dt = 0.002,  ! Timestep [ps] (2 fs)
ntc = 2, ntf = 2,  ! Shake ON for H
{% else %}
dt = 0.001,  ! Timestep [ps] (1 fs) 
ntc = 1, ntf = 1,  ! Shake OFF
{% endif %}
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:12-18](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:33-47]()

## Template Variable Reference

### Common Variables

| Variable | Type | Purpose | Used In |
|----------|------|---------|---------|
| `tstep_num` | Integer | Number of simulation steps | Both templates |
| `dump_traj` | Boolean | Enable trajectory output | Both templates |
| `cutoff` | Float | Non-bonded cutoff distance | Scaling template |
| `cuda` | Boolean | Enable GPU acceleration | Both templates |

### ML/MM Specific Variables

| Variable | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `mlmm.selection` | String | QM atom selection mask |
| `mlmm.cutoff` | Float | QM-MM interaction cutoff |
| `mlmm.protocol` | String | Coupling protocol type |
| `mlmm.cuda` | Boolean | GPU usage for QM region |
| `mlmm.float64` | Boolean | Double precision for QM |
| `mlmm.use_torch_coupling` | Boolean | Use PyTorch for coupling |

### Scaling Specific Variables

| Variable | Type | Purpose |
|----------|------|---------|
| `cuaev` | Boolean | Enable cuAEV optimization |
| `model` | String | Neural network model name |
| `shake` | Boolean | Enable SHAKE constraints |
| `use_amber_neighborlist` | Boolean | Use Amber neighborlist |
| `use_all_amber_nonbond` | Boolean | Use all Amber non-bonded terms |

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:4](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:7](), [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:36-58](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:37-46]()

## Common Simulation Examples

### Example 1: Basic ML/MM Simulation

Template variables for a simple alanine dipeptide ML/MM simulation:

```python
{
    "tstep_num": 1000,
    "dump_traj": False,
    "mlmm": {
        "selection": ":1-3",
        "cutoff": 8.0,
        "protocol": "ani_me", 
        "cuda": True,
        "float64": False,
        "use_torch_coupling": True
    }
}
```

### Example 2: Performance Scaling Study

Template variables for benchmarking with cuAEV optimization:

```python
{
    "tstep_num": 100,
    "dump_traj": False,
    "cutoff": 8.0,
    "cuda": True,
    "cuaev": True,
    "model": "ani2x",
    "shake": True,
    "use_amber_neighborlist": True
}
```

### Example 3: Development Testing with Full Output

Template variables for debugging with complete trajectory output:

```python
{
    "tstep_num": 10,
    "dump_traj": True,
    "mlmm": {
        "selection": ":1-9",
        "cutoff": 8.0,
        "protocol": "ani_mbispol",
        "cuda": False,
        "float64": True,
        "use_torch_coupling": False
    }
}
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:15](), [benchmark/templates/scaling.mdin.jinja:13](), [benchmark/templates/mlmm.mdin.jinja:21-27]()

# Page: Benchmarking System

# Benchmarking System

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [benchmark/bench](benchmark/bench)
- [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja](benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja)

</details>



The benchmarking system provides a comprehensive framework for performance testing and scaling studies of TorchANI-Amber simulations. It enables automated execution of molecular dynamics simulations across different system sizes, neural network models, and hardware configurations, with integrated analysis and visualization tools.

For information about configuring individual simulations, see [Simulation Configuration](#4.1). For details about the command-line interface specifically, see [Bench CLI Tool](#5.1).

## System Architecture

The benchmarking framework consists of a Python-based CLI tool that orchestrates simulation execution, data collection, and performance analysis across both local and HPC environments.

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Benchmarking Frontend"
        CLI["bench CLI Tool"]
        CONFIG["ScalingConfig"]
        TEMPLATES["Jinja2 Templates"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Execution Environment"
        LOCAL["Local Execution"]
        HPC["HPC/SLURM Execution"]
        SCHEDULER["send_to_scheduler()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Simulation Systems"
        WATER["Water Box Systems"]
        SIZES["1k - 200k atoms"]
        FILES["prmtop/inpcrd files"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Models & Configuration"
        MODELS["Neural Network Models"]
        ANI["ANI variants"]
        AIMNET["AimNet2"]
        NUTMEG["NutMeg"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Output & Analysis"
        TIMING["walltime_ms.dat"]
        RESULTS["Performance Data"]
        PLOTS["Scaling Plots"]
        CSV["CSV Reports"]
    end
    
    CLI --> CONFIG
    CLI --> TEMPLATES
    CLI --> LOCAL
    CLI --> SCHEDULER
    SCHEDULER --> HPC
    
    CONFIG --> MODELS
    TEMPLATES --> WATER
    WATER --> SIZES
    SIZES --> FILES
    
    LOCAL --> TIMING
    HPC --> TIMING
    TIMING --> RESULTS
    RESULTS --> PLOTS
    RESULTS --> CSV
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:1-471]()

## Benchmark Types and Configuration

The system supports different benchmark types through the `BenchKind` enum and configurable parameters via the `ScalingConfig` dataclass.

### Benchmark Categories

| Benchmark Type | Purpose | Implementation Status |
|----------------|---------|----------------------|
| `SCALING` | Performance scaling across system sizes | Implemented |
| `REMD` | Replica Exchange MD benchmarks | Not implemented |

### Configuration Parameters

The `ScalingConfig` dataclass defines the core benchmark parameters:

```mermaid
graph LR
    subgraph "ScalingConfig Parameters"
        CUAEV["cuaev: bool"]
        CUDA["cuda: bool"] 
        CUTOFF["cutoff: float"]
        TSTEPS["tstep_num: int"]
        MODEL["model: str"]
        SHAKE["shake: bool"]
        TRAJ["dump_traj: bool"]
        AMBER_NB["use_all_amber_nonbond: bool"]
        AMBER_NL["use_amber_neighborlist: bool"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model-Specific Defaults"
        ANI_CUTOFF["ANI models: 5.2 Å"]
        ANI2DR_CUTOFF["ani2dr: 8.0 Å"] 
        AIMNET_CUTOFF["AimNet2/NutMeg: 10.0 Å"]
    end
    
    CUTOFF --> ANI_CUTOFF
    CUTOFF --> ANI2DR_CUTOFF
    CUTOFF --> AIMNET_CUTOFF
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:33-52](), [benchmark/bench:241-247]()

## Execution Workflow

The benchmark execution follows a structured workflow that handles both local and HPC environments:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    START["bench run command"]
    DETECT["Detect execution environment"]
    
    subgraph "Environment Detection"
        LOCAL_CHECK["Check --hpg flag"]
        HOSTNAME_CHECK["Check hostname pattern"]
        HPC_DECISION{"Execute on HPC?"}
    end
    
    subgraph "HPC Execution Path"
        SLURM_TEMPLATE["Load hpg.slurm.sh.jinja"]
        SUBMIT_JOB["Submit SLURM job"]
        SCHEDULER_EXEC["Execute via send_to_scheduler()"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Local Execution Path"
        SETUP_ENV["Set TORCHANI_AMBER_WALLTIME=1"]
        ITERATE_SYSTEMS["Iterate through systems"]
        GENERATE_MDIN["Generate mdin from template"]
        COPY_FILES["Copy prmtop/inpcrd files"]
        RUN_AMBER["Execute sander/pmemd"]
        COLLECT_TIMING["Collect timing data"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Results Processing"
        WALLTIME_DATA["walltime_ms.dat files"]
        CONFIG_JSON["config.json files"]
        OUTPUT_DIR["Organized output directory"]
    end
    
    START --> DETECT
    DETECT --> LOCAL_CHECK
    LOCAL_CHECK --> HOSTNAME_CHECK
    HOSTNAME_CHECK --> HPC_DECISION
    
    HPC_DECISION -->|Yes| SLURM_TEMPLATE
    SLURM_TEMPLATE --> SUBMIT_JOB
    SUBMIT_JOB --> SCHEDULER_EXEC
    
    HPC_DECISION -->|No| SETUP_ENV
    SETUP_ENV --> ITERATE_SYSTEMS
    ITERATE_SYSTEMS --> GENERATE_MDIN
    GENERATE_MDIN --> COPY_FILES
    COPY_FILES --> RUN_AMBER
    RUN_AMBER --> COLLECT_TIMING
    
    SCHEDULER_EXEC --> WALLTIME_DATA
    COLLECT_TIMING --> WALLTIME_DATA
    WALLTIME_DATA --> CONFIG_JSON
    CONFIG_JSON --> OUTPUT_DIR
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:224-237](), [benchmark/bench:278-307]()

## HPC Integration

The system provides sophisticated HPC integration through SLURM templates and environment management:

### SLURM Configuration

| Parameter | Purpose | Configuration |
|-----------|---------|---------------|
| `job-name` | Job identification | `{{ unique_id }}-v{{ version }}-{{ name }}` |
| `partition` | Queue selection | Configurable via `--gpu` parameter |
| `gres` | GPU resources | `gpu:{{ gpu }}` specification |
| `time` | Walltime limit | `{{ hours }}:00:00` format |
| `nodes` | Node allocation | Fixed at 1 node |
| `cpus-per-task` | CPU cores | Fixed at 1 core |

### Environment Management

The SLURM template supports multiple installation configurations:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Installation Types"
        MODULES["modules: Shared module system"]
        LOCAL["local: User conda environment"]
        SHARED["shared-env: Shared conda environment"]
        BLACKWELL["b200:1: Blackwell GPU support"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Module Loading"
        CUDA["CUDA modules"]
        GCC["GCC compiler"]
        MPI["OpenMPI"]
        CONDA["Conda environment"]
        CMAKE["CMake build system"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Environment Activation"
        AMBER_ENV["Amber environment"]
        CONDA_ACT["Conda activation"]
        MAMBA_ACT["Mamba activation"]
    end
    
    MODULES --> CUDA
    MODULES --> GCC
    MODULES --> MPI
    MODULES --> CONDA
    MODULES --> CMAKE
    
    LOCAL --> CONDA_ACT
    LOCAL --> MAMBA_ACT
    
    SHARED --> CONDA_ACT
    SHARED --> AMBER_ENV
    
    BLACKWELL --> CUDA
    BLACKWELL --> MAMBA_ACT
```

Sources: [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja:1-32]()

## Performance Analysis and Visualization

The benchmarking system includes comprehensive analysis capabilities through the `plot` command:

### Data Processing Pipeline

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Raw Data"
        WALLTIME["walltime_ms.dat"]
        INPCRD["inpcrd files"]
        CONFIG["config.json"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Processing Steps"
        PARSE["Parse timing data"]
        BURNIN["Apply burn-in filter"]
        ATOMS["Extract atom counts"]
        STATS["Calculate statistics"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Metrics Calculation"
        MEAN["Mean walltime per step"]
        STD["Standard deviation"]
        NSDAY["ns/day conversion"]
        SCALING["Scaling analysis"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Visualization"
        SCATTER["Scatter plots"]
        TREND["Trend lines"]
        CSV_OUT["CSV export"]
        PLOTS["Interactive plots"]
    end
    
    WALLTIME --> PARSE
    INPCRD --> ATOMS
    PARSE --> BURNIN
    BURNIN --> STATS
    ATOMS --> STATS
    
    STATS --> MEAN
    STATS --> STD
    MEAN --> NSDAY
    NSDAY --> SCALING
    
    SCALING --> SCATTER
    SCALING --> TREND
    SCALING --> CSV_OUT
    SCATTER --> PLOTS
```

### Performance Metrics

The system generates two primary performance metrics:

| Metric | Units | Calculation | Purpose |
|--------|-------|-------------|---------|
| Walltime per timestep | milliseconds | Direct measurement | Low-level performance |
| Simulation rate | ns/day | `86.4 / walltime_ms` | Production throughput |

Sources: [benchmark/bench:309-467](), [benchmark/bench:441-444]()

## Model Support and Optimization

The benchmarking framework supports multiple neural network models with model-specific optimizations:

### Supported Models

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "ANI Model Family"
        ANI1X["ani1x"]
        ANI2X["ani2x"] 
        ANI2XR["ani2xr"]
        ANI2DR["ani2dr"]
    end
    
    subgraph "AimNet2 Models"
        AIMNET_BASE["aimnet2-wb97m-dsf"]
        AIMNET_VARIANTS["AimNet2 variants"]
    end
    
    subgraph "NutMeg Models"
        NUTMEG_SMALL["nutmeg-small"]
        NUTMEG_VARIANTS["NutMeg variants"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Model-Specific Features"
        CUAEV_SUPPORT["CUAEV acceleration"]
        CHARGE_PRED["Charge prediction"]
        CUTOFF_OPT["Cutoff optimization"]
    end
    
    ANI1X --> CUAEV_SUPPORT
    ANI2X --> CUAEV_SUPPORT
    ANI2XR --> CUAEV_SUPPORT
    ANI2DR --> CUTOFF_OPT
    
    AIMNET_BASE --> CHARGE_PRED
    NUTMEG_SMALL --> CHARGE_PRED
```

### Hardware Optimization

The system automatically detects and configures hardware-specific optimizations:

| Feature | Detection Method | Configuration |
|---------|------------------|---------------|
| CUDA availability | `torch.cuda.is_available()` | Automatic GPU usage |
| CUAEV acceleration | Model name pattern matching | ANI models only |
| Amber neighborlist | User configuration | Optional optimization |
| Amber nonbonded | User configuration | Performance trade-off |

Sources: [benchmark/bench:26](), [benchmark/bench:156-158](), [benchmark/bench:239-252](), [benchmark/bench:282-285]()

# Page: Bench CLI Tool

# Bench CLI Tool

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [benchmark/bench](benchmark/bench)
- [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja](benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja)

</details>



The `bench` CLI tool provides a comprehensive benchmarking framework for TorchANI-Amber molecular dynamics simulations. It automates the execution of scaling studies and performance analysis across different system sizes, neural network models, and hardware configurations. The tool supports both local execution and HPC cluster submission with SLURM scheduling.

For information about interpreting benchmark results and performance metrics, see [Performance Testing and Analysis](#5.2).

## CLI Commands Overview

The `bench` tool provides two primary commands implemented using the Typer framework:

| Command | Purpose | Key Options |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `run` | Execute benchmark simulations | `--model`, `--systems`, `--hpg`, `--tsteps` |
| `plot` | Generate performance plots from results | `--ns-per-day`, `--burn-in-tstep-num`, `--labels` |

**CLI Application Structure**
```mermaid
graph TB
    app["app: Typer(name='bench')"]
    app --> run_cmd["run() command"]
    app --> plot_cmd["plot() command"]
    
    run_cmd --> local_exec["Local Execution"]
    run_cmd --> hpg_submit["HPC Submission"]
    
    plot_cmd --> data_analysis["_plot_single()"]
    plot_cmd --> matplotlib_output["Performance Plots"]
    
    local_exec --> amber_sim["Amber MD Simulation"]
    hpg_submit --> slurm_sched["SLURM Scheduler"]
    
    slurm_sched --> remote_exec["Remote Execution"]
    remote_exec --> amber_sim
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:21-31](), [benchmark/bench:54-150](), [benchmark/bench:309-340]()

## Run Command

The `run` command orchestrates benchmark execution with extensive configuration options for different simulation scenarios.

### Core Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|-----------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--model` | str | "ani2xr" | Neural network model to benchmark |
| `--tsteps` | int | 1000 | Number of MD timesteps to execute |
| `--systems` | List[str] | Auto-detected | System sizes for scaling studies |
| `--hpg` | bool | Auto-detected | Enable HPC cluster submission |
| `--cuda` | bool | Auto-detected | Use CUDA acceleration |

### Benchmark Types

The tool supports different benchmark kinds through the `BenchKind` enum:

```mermaid
graph LR
    bench_kind["--bench-kind"]
    bench_kind --> scaling["BenchKind.SCALING"]
    bench_kind --> remd["BenchKind.REMD"]
    
    scaling --> water_systems["Water box systems<br/>1k-200k atoms"]
    remd --> not_impl["NotImplementedError"]
    
    water_systems --> template["scaling.mdin.jinja"]
```

The scaling benchmark automatically selects water box systems ranging from 1,000 to 200,000 atoms when no specific systems are provided [benchmark/bench:177-200]().

### Configuration Management

Benchmark parameters are managed through the `ScalingConfig` dataclass:

```mermaid
graph TB
    config["ScalingConfig"]
    config --> cuaev["cuaev: bool"]
    config --> cuda["cuda: bool"] 
    config --> cutoff["cutoff: float"]
    config --> tstep_num["tstep_num: int"]
    config --> model["model: str"]
    config --> shake["shake: bool"]
    config --> dump_traj["dump_traj: bool"]
    config --> amber_nb["use_all_amber_nonbond: bool"]
    config --> amber_nl["use_amber_neighborlist: bool"]
    
    config --> json_export["to_json_file()"]
    json_export --> config_json["config.json"]
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:38-52](), [benchmark/bench:264-274]()

### Execution Workflow

**Local vs HPC Execution Decision Tree**
```mermaid
graph TD
    start["bench run command"]
    start --> hpg_check{"--hpg specified?"}
    
    hpg_check -->|No| hostname_check{"hostname matches<br/>login*.ufhpc?"}
    hpg_check -->|Yes| hpg_true["hpg = True"]
    
    hostname_check -->|Yes| hpg_auto["hpg = True"]
    hostname_check -->|No| hpg_false["hpg = False"]
    
    hpg_true --> slurm_submit["send_to_scheduler()"]
    hpg_auto --> slurm_submit
    hpg_false --> local_exec["Local execution"]
    
    slurm_submit --> sys_exit["sys.exit(0)"]
    
    local_exec --> setup_dirs["Setup output directories"]
    setup_dirs --> system_loop["Iterate over systems"]
    system_loop --> render_mdin["Render mdin template"]
    render_mdin --> copy_files["Copy .prmtop/.inpcrd"]
    copy_files --> run_amber["subprocess.run(cmd)"]
    run_amber --> check_result{"Success?"}
    check_result -->|No| error_output["Print error and break"]
    check_result -->|Yes| next_system["Next system"]
```

Sources: [benchmark/bench:224-237](), [benchmark/bench:280-307]()

## Plot Command

The `plot` command generates performance visualizations from benchmark output data.

### Key Options

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
|--------|------|---------|-------------|
| `--burn-in-tstep-num` | int | 50 | Skip initial timesteps in analysis |
| `--ns-per-day` | bool | False | Plot simulation speed vs walltime |
| `--labels` | List[str] | Auto-generated | Custom labels for plot series |
| `--max-num-atoms` | int | 1e12 | Filter systems by atom count |

### Data Processing Pipeline

```mermaid
graph LR
    input_paths["names_or_paths"]
    input_paths --> path_resolution["Resolve paths in ~/IO/ani-amber"]
    
    path_resolution --> system_dirs["System directories"]
    system_dirs --> walltime_data["walltime_ms.dat"]
    system_dirs --> inpcrd_data["inpcrd (atom count)"]
    
    walltime_data --> burn_in["Apply burn-in filter"]
    burn_in --> stats["Calculate mean/std"]
    
    inpcrd_data --> atom_count["Extract num_atoms"]
    
    stats --> plot_data["Plotting data"]
    atom_count --> plot_data
    
    plot_data --> matplotlib_viz["matplotlib visualization"]
    plot_data --> csv_export["CSV export"]
```

The plotting function automatically converts walltime measurements to ns/day performance metrics using the conversion factor `86.4 / means` [benchmark/bench:441-444]().

Sources: [benchmark/bench:309-385](), [benchmark/bench:387-467]()

## HPC Integration

The tool integrates with SLURM schedulers through the `send_to_scheduler` function and Jinja2 templates.

### SLURM Template System

```mermaid
graph TB
    hpg_template["hpg.slurm.sh.jinja"]
    hpg_template --> sbatch_directives["SBATCH directives"]
    hpg_template --> module_loading["Module loading"]
    hpg_template --> env_activation["Environment activation"]
    hpg_template --> bench_execution["bench command execution"]
    
    sbatch_directives --> job_name["--job-name={{ unique_id }}-v{{ version }}-{{ name }}"]
    sbatch_directives --> gpu_resources["--gres=gpu:{{ gpu }}"]
    sbatch_directives --> time_limit["--time={{ hours }}:00:00"]
    
    module_loading --> cuda_mod["CUDA modules"]
    module_loading --> conda_mod["Conda modules"]
    
    env_activation --> install_kinds["Different install_kind options"]
    install_kinds --> modules_env["modules: shared benchmark env"]
    install_kinds --> local_env["local: user conda env"]
    install_kinds --> shared_env["shared-env: group environment"]
```

The template supports multiple installation configurations based on the `install_kind` parameter [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja:17-29]().

### GPU Resource Management

| GPU Type | CUDA Version | Environment |
|----------|--------------|-------------|
| `b200:1` | 12.8 | ani-amber-blackwell |
| Standard | 12.4 | ani-amber-bench |
| Shared | 12.4 | ani-amber-gcc1104-cuda1204 |

Sources: [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja:1-32](), [benchmark/bench:227-236]()

## Configuration and Templates

### Jinja2 Template Environment

The tool uses a Jinja2 environment configured for strict template processing:

```mermaid
graph LR
    jinja_env["jinja2.Environment"]
    jinja_env --> loader["FileSystemLoader"]
    jinja_env --> strict["StrictUndefined"]
    jinja_env --> autoescape["select_autoescape()"]
    jinja_env --> formatting["trim_blocks + lstrip_blocks"]
    
    loader --> templates_dir["benchmark/templates/"]
    templates_dir --> scaling_template["scaling.mdin.jinja"]
    templates_dir --> slurm_template["hpg.slurm.sh.jinja"]
    
    strict --> template_vars["Template variable validation"]
    autoescape --> security["XSS protection"]
```

### Model-Specific Configuration

The tool automatically configures cutoff distances and CUAEV settings based on the selected model:

| Model Pattern | Cutoff (Å) | CUAEV Enabled |
|---------------|------------|---------------|
| `ani2dr` | 8.0 | True |
| `nutmeg*` | 10.0 | False |
| `aimnet*` | 10.0 | False |
| Default | 5.2 | True for `ani*` models |

Special handling exists for NutMeg models, which require charge file specification [benchmark/bench:282-285]().

Sources: [benchmark/bench:161-167](), [benchmark/bench:239-247](), [benchmark/bench:282-285]()

## Output Management

### Directory Structure

```mermaid
graph TB
    out_root["~/IO/ani-amber/"]
    out_root --> unique_dir["{{ unique_id }}-{{ name }}/"]
    
    unique_dir --> system_dirs["System directories"]
    system_dirs --> water_1k["water-1k/"]
    system_dirs --> water_2_5k["water-2_5k/"]
    system_dirs --> water_etc["..."]
    
    water_1k --> mdin_file["mdin"]
    water_1k --> config_file["config.json"]
    water_1k --> input_files["inpcrd, prmtop"]
    water_1k --> output_files["Output files"]
    
    output_files --> walltime_dat["walltime_ms.dat"]
    output_files --> amber_out["mdout, mdcrd, etc."]
```

### Environment Variables

The tool sets `TORCHANI_AMBER_WALLTIME=1` to enable walltime measurement collection from the Amber integration [benchmark/bench:278]().

### Performance Data Collection

Walltime data is collected per timestep and written to `walltime_ms.dat` files. The plotting system processes this data with configurable burn-in periods to exclude initialization overhead from performance analysis.

Sources: [benchmark/bench:254-259](), [benchmark/bench:288-294](), [benchmark/bench:418-433]()

# Page: Performance Testing and Analysis

# Performance Testing and Analysis

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [benchmark/bench](benchmark/bench)
- [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja](benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja)
- [tests/test_values_cpu_1ccx_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cpu_1ccx_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cpu_1x_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cpu_1x_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cpu_2x_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cpu_2x_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cpu_mbis_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cpu_mbis_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cuda_1ccx_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cuda_1ccx_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cuda_1x_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cuda_1x_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cuda_2x_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cuda_2x_ensemble.txt)
- [tests/test_values_cuda_mbis_ensemble.txt](tests/test_values_cuda_mbis_ensemble.txt)

</details>



This page covers the performance testing and analysis capabilities of TorchANI-Amber, focusing on how to conduct scaling studies, interpret benchmark results, and generate performance visualizations. For information about the bench CLI tool itself and basic usage, see [Bench CLI Tool](#5.1).

## Purpose and Scope

The performance testing system provides comprehensive tools for analyzing TorchANI-Amber's computational performance across different system sizes, hardware configurations, and model types. The analysis framework supports:

- Scaling studies across different molecular system sizes
- Performance comparison between different neural network models
- Hardware performance analysis (CPU vs GPU, different GPU types)
- HPC cluster scaling analysis
- Automated visualization and reporting

Sources: [benchmark/bench:1-470]()

## Scaling Study Workflow

The typical scaling study workflow involves running benchmarks across multiple system sizes and then analyzing the results to understand performance characteristics.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Configure scaling study] --> B["bench run --bench-kind scaling"]
    B --> C["Execute across system sizes"]
    C --> D["Collect walltime_ms.dat files"]
    D --> E["Generate performance plots"]
    E --> F["Analyze scaling behavior"]
    
    subgraph "System sizes"
        G["water-1k"]
        H["water-5k"] 
        I["water-10k"]
        J["water-25k"]
        K["water-100k+"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Analysis outputs"
        L["Performance plots"]
        M["CSV data files"]
        N["ns/day metrics"]
    end
    
    C --> G
    C --> H
    C --> I
    C --> J
    C --> K
    
    E --> L
    E --> M
    E --> N
```

The scaling study automatically tests predefined system sizes ranging from 1,000 to 200,000 atoms, allowing comprehensive performance characterization.

Sources: [benchmark/bench:169-200](), [benchmark/bench:277-307]()

## Benchmark Data Structure

Each benchmark execution generates a structured output directory containing performance data and configuration information:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["benchmark-output-dir/"] --> B["unique-id-model-name/"]
    B --> C["water-1k/"]
    B --> D["water-5k/"]
    B --> E["water-10k/"]
    
    C --> F["walltime_ms.dat"]
    C --> G["config.json"]
    C --> H["mdin"]
    C --> I["inpcrd"]
    C --> J["prmtop"]
    C --> K["mdout"]
    
    D --> L["walltime_ms.dat"]
    D --> M["config.json"]
    E --> N["walltime_ms.dat"]
    E --> O["config.json"]
```

**Key Data Files:**

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `walltime_ms.dat` | Per-timestep walltime measurements in milliseconds |
| `config.json` | ScalingConfig parameters for reproducibility |
| `mdin` | Generated Amber input file |
| `mdout` | Amber simulation output |

The `walltime_ms.dat` file contains one measurement per line, with each value representing the walltime for a single MD timestep.

Sources: [benchmark/bench:418-421](), [benchmark/bench:291-294]()

## Performance Visualization

The plotting system provides automated visualization of benchmark results with multiple analysis modes:

### Basic Performance Plotting

```bash
bench plot ani2xr-scaling aimnet2-scaling --label "ANI-2xr" --label "AimNet2"
```

### Throughput Analysis

```bash
bench plot ani2xr-scaling --ns-per-day --ymax 6
```

The plotting system generates two key metrics:

```mermaid
graph LR
    A["walltime_ms.dat"] --> B["Walltime per timestep (ms)"]
    A --> C["ns/day calculation"]
    
    B --> D["Performance comparison"]
    C --> E["Throughput analysis"]
    
    F["Formula: 86.4 / walltime_ms"] --> C
```

**Performance Metrics:**

| Metric | Formula | Purpose |
|--------|---------|---------|
| Walltime per timestep | Direct from data | Raw performance measurement |
| ns/day throughput | `86.4 / walltime_ms` | Simulation productivity metric |

Sources: [benchmark/bench:441-445](), [benchmark/bench:324-327]()

## Statistical Analysis and Burn-in

The analysis system incorporates statistical rigor through burn-in periods and error analysis:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Raw walltime data"] --> B["Apply burn-in filter"]
    B --> C["Calculate statistics"]
    C --> D["Mean walltime"]
    C --> E["Standard deviation"]
    
    F["burn_in_tstep_num=50"] --> B
    
    D --> G["Performance plots"]
    E --> H["Error bars"]
```

The system automatically:
- Excludes initial timesteps (default: 50) to account for initialization overhead
- Calculates mean and standard deviation for each system size
- Generates CSV output with statistical summaries

Sources: [benchmark/bench:421-433](), [benchmark/bench:460-466]()

## Model and Hardware Performance Analysis

The benchmarking system supports comparative analysis across different configurations:

### Model Comparison Framework

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["ScalingConfig parameters"] --> B["Model selection"]
    A --> C["Hardware configuration"] 
    A --> D["Optimization settings"]
    
    B --> E["ani1x, ani2x, ani2xr"]
    B --> F["aimnet2-wb97m-dsf"]
    B --> G["nutmeg variants"]
    
    C --> H["CUDA vs CPU"]
    C --> I["cuAEV acceleration"]
    
    D --> J["Amber neighborlist"]
    D --> K["Amber nonbonded"]
    D --> L["SHAKE constraints"]
```

**Key Configuration Parameters:**

| Parameter | Options | Impact |
|-----------|---------|--------|
| `cuaev` | true/false | Enables CUDA-accelerated AEV computation |
| `cuda` | true/false | GPU vs CPU execution |
| `use_amber_neighborlist` | true/false | Amber vs TorchANI neighbor detection |
| `use_all_amber_nonbond` | true/false | Hybrid force calculation |
| `shake` | true/false | Bond constraint algorithm |

Sources: [benchmark/bench:39-48](), [benchmark/bench:239-247]()

## HPC Scaling Analysis

For large-scale performance studies, the system integrates with HPC schedulers:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant CLI as "bench CLI"
    participant SLURM as "HPC Scheduler"
    participant Compute as "Compute Nodes"
    
    User->>CLI: bench run --hpg
    CLI->>SLURM: Submit job via template
    SLURM->>Compute: Allocate resources
    Compute->>Compute: Execute scaling study
    Compute->>CLI: Return results
    CLI->>User: Performance data
```

The HPC integration automatically:
- Detects HPC environment based on hostname pattern
- Submits jobs via SLURM templates
- Manages environment modules and conda activation
- Handles GPU resource allocation

Sources: [benchmark/bench:224-237](), [benchmark/templates/hpg.slurm.sh.jinja:1-32]()

## Automated Analysis Pipeline

A complete performance analysis typically follows this pipeline:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Define test systems"] --> B["Execute scaling study"]
    B --> C["Collect performance data"]
    C --> D["Generate visualizations"]
    D --> E["Export CSV data"]
    E --> F["Analyze scaling trends"]
    
    subgraph "Quality control"
        G["Burn-in filtering"]
        H["Statistical validation"]
        I["Outlier detection"]
    end
    
    C --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> D
    
    subgraph "Output products"
        J["Performance plots"]
        K["CSV datasets"]
        L["Scaling coefficients"]
    end
    
    D --> J
    E --> K
    F --> L
```

The system ensures reproducibility by:
- Saving complete configuration in `config.json`
- Using consistent system definitions
- Applying standardized analysis methods
- Generating machine-readable output formats

Sources: [benchmark/bench:264-274](), [benchmark/bench:413-466]()

This guide provides essential information for developers contributing to TorchANI-Amber, covering the development environment, build system, testing infrastructure, and contribution workflow. This document focuses on the technical aspects of working with the codebase and build system.

For detailed build system configuration options, see [Build System Deep Dive](#6.1). For comprehensive testing procedures and framework details, see [Testing Framework](#6.2). For development workflow and code quality standards, see [Code Quality and Development Workflow](#6.3).

## Development Environment Setup

TorchANI-Amber requires a carefully configured development environment due to its complex dependency chain involving PyTorch, CUDA, cuDNN, and Amber molecular dynamics engines.

### Conda Environment Configuration

The project uses a conda environment specification that ensures compatibility across all components:

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "Base Dependencies"
        PYTHON["python=3.11"]
        PYTORCH["pytorch=2.5"]
        NUMPY["numpy=1.26"]

        CUDA_LIBS["cuda-libraries-dev=12.4"]
        CUDA_NVCC["cuda-nvcc=12.4"]
        CUDNN["cudnn"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Compilers"

        GFORTRAN["gfortran_linux-64=12.2"]
```

The environment enforces strict version compatibility, particularly for the CUDA stack where PyTorch 2.5 must match CUDA 12.4 and the corresponding cuDNN version.

### Key Computational Modules

The `electro` namespace provides core electrostatic calculation functionality:

- `coulombic_embedding_energy()`: Calculates Coulombic QM/MM interaction energy
- `polarizable_embedding_energy()`: Computes polarizable embedding energy using atomic polarizabilities

Sources: [src/electro.h:4-18](), [src/electro.cpp:78-89]()

## Development Workflow

### Build Process

1. **Environment Setup**: Activate the `ani-amber` conda environment
2. **Configuration**: Run CMake with appropriate options for your development setup
3. **Compilation**: Build the shared libraries and test executables
4. **Testing**: Execute the test suite to validate functionality

### Common Development Scenarios

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "Development Tasks"
        NEW_FEATURE["New Feature"]
        BUG_FIX["Bug Fix"]
        PERF_OPT["Performance Optimization"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Workflow Steps"
        BRANCH["Create Branch"]
        CODE["Code Changes"]
        BUILD["Build & Test"]
        VALIDATE["Integration Tests"]
        PR["Pull Request"]
    end
    
    NEW_FEATURE --> BRANCH
    BUG_FIX --> BRANCH
    PERF_OPT --> BRANCH
    
    BRANCH --> CODE
    CODE --> BUILD
    BUILD --> VALIDATE
    VALIDATE --> PR
```

### Testing Strategy

The testing approach validates both individual components and full system integration:

- **Unit Tests**: C++ components tested with Catch2 framework
- **Integration Tests**: Full Amber MD simulations with expected output comparison
- **Configuration Tests**: Parameterized testing across CUDA/CPU, ML/MM modes
- **Regression Tests**: Automated comparison against reference outputs

Sources: [tests/test_amber_integration.py:127-383]()

The development environment supports rapid iteration through automated build configuration detection and comprehensive test coverage across deployment scenarios.

# Page: Build System Deep Dive

# Build System Deep Dive

<details>
<summary>Relevant source files</summary>

The following files were used as context for generating this wiki page:

- [CMakeLists.txt](CMakeLists.txt)
- [cmake/Msg.cmake](cmake/Msg.cmake)
- [cmake/TorchaniConfig.cmake.in](cmake/TorchaniConfig.cmake.in)
- [cmake/detect_pytorch.py](cmake/detect_pytorch.py)
- [environment.yaml](environment.yaml)

</details>



This document provides a comprehensive overview of the CMake-based build system used in TorchANI-Amber. It covers the build configuration process, dependency resolution, target compilation, and installation procedures. For information about using the build artifacts in simulations, see [Amber Integration](#4). For testing the build outputs, see [Testing Framework](#6.2).

## Build System Architecture

The TorchANI-Amber build system is implemented as a sophisticated CMake project that manages complex dependencies including PyTorch/LibTorch, CUDA toolkit, cuDNN, and Python extensions. The system supports multiple build configurations and deployment scenarios.

### Build Process Overview

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["CMakeLists.txt"] --> B["Configuration Validation"]
    B --> C["Environment Detection"]
    C --> D["Dependency Resolution"]
    D --> E["JIT Model Compilation"]
    E --> F["Target Compilation"]
    F --> G["Testing Integration"]
    G --> H["Installation & Packaging"]
    
    B --> B1["Option Validation"]
    B --> B2["Compiler Verification"]
    
    C --> C1["Conda Environment"]
    C --> C2["PyTorch Detection"]
    
    D --> D1["LibTorch/PyTorch"]
    D --> D2["CUDA Toolkit"]
    D --> D3["cuDNN Library"]
    D --> D4["Python Headers"]
    
    F --> F1["libcell_list.so"]
    F --> F2["libcuaev.so"]
    F --> F3["libtorchani.so"]
    
    H --> H1["CMake Config Files"]
    H --> H2["Shared Libraries"]
    H --> H3["Include Headers"]
    H --> H4["Fortran Interface"]
```

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:1-462]()

### Configuration Options and Flags

The build system provides extensive configuration through CMake options that control dependency handling and compilation behavior:

| Option | Default | Description |
|--------|---------|-------------|
| `LINK_TO_PYTORCH_LIBS` | ON | Link to existing PyTorch installation |
| `DOWNLOAD_AND_INSTALL_LIBTORCH` | OFF | Download LibTorch if PyTorch unavailable |
| `PREFER_CONDA_LIBS` | ON | Prioritize libraries from active conda environment |
| `COMPILE_WITH_CXX11ABI` | OFF | Use C++11 ABI (requires LibTorch mode) |
| `USE_CUSTOM_CUDNN` | OFF | Use cuDNN from `./external/cudnn<version>` |
| `USE_CUSTOM_CUDATK` | OFF | Use CUDA Toolkit from `/usr/local/cuda-<version>` |
| `JIT_COMPILE_MODELS` | ON | JIT-compile ANI models during build |
| `JIT_FORCE_RECOMPILATION` | OFF | Force recompilation of existing `.pt` files |
| `SET_TORCHANI_LIBRARIES_INSTALL_RPATH` | ON | Set RPATH for installed libraries |

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:38-46](), [CMakeLists.txt:91-93]()

### Dependency Resolution Workflow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph "PyTorch Detection"
        A["detect_pytorch.py"] --> B["Extract Versions"]
        B --> C["Validate Compatibility"]
        C --> D["Set CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH"]
    end
    
    subgraph "CUDA Setup"
        E["Environment Check"] --> F{"Conda or Custom?"}
        F -->|Conda| G["CudaToolkitHelper_set_conda_paths"]
        F -->|Custom| H["CudaToolkitHelper_set_custom_paths"]
        G --> I["Set CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR"]
        H --> I
    end
    
    subgraph "cuDNN Setup"
        J["cuDNN Detection"] --> K{"Source Location?"}
        K -->|Conda| L["CudnnHelper_set_conda_paths"]
        K -->|Custom| M["CudnnHelper_set_custom_paths"]
        K -->|System| N["Use CUDA Toolkit Dir"]
        L --> O["Set CUDNN_LIBRARY"]
        M --> O
        N --> O
    end
    
    D --> P["find_package(Torch)"]
    I --> P
    O --> P
```

The dependency resolution process handles three critical components:

**PyTorch/LibTorch Detection**: The system uses [cmake/detect_pytorch.py:1-16]() to extract version information and installation paths from an existing PyTorch installation. This script extracts torch version, CUDA version, cuDNN version, and the PyTorch root directory.

**CUDA Toolkit Resolution**: Depending on configuration, the system either uses CUDA from the active conda environment or searches custom paths. The `CudaToolkitHelper` modules set `CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR` and `CMAKE_CUDA_COMPILER` variables.

**cuDNN Library Management**: Similar to CUDA, cuDNN can be sourced from conda, custom directories, or assumed to be co-located with the CUDA Toolkit.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:115-165](), [CMakeLists.txt:167-186](), [CMakeLists.txt:188-212](), [cmake/detect_pytorch.py:1-16]()

## Target Compilation Process

### Library Target Hierarchy

```mermaid
graph TB
    subgraph "External Dependencies"
        TORCH["${TORCH_LIBRARIES}"]
        PYTHON["${Python_LIBRARIES}"]
        CUDA["CUDA Runtime"]
    end
    
    subgraph "TorchANI Libraries"
        CELL["cell_list"]
        CUAEV["cuaev"] 
        TORCHANI["torchani"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Source Locations"
        CELL_SRC["submodules/torchani_sandbox/torchani/csrc/cell_list.cpp"]
        CUAEV_SRC["submodules/torchani_sandbox/torchani/csrc/cuaev.cpp<br/>submodules/torchani_sandbox/torchani/csrc/aev.cu"]
        TORCHANI_SRC["src/*.cpp"]
    end
    
    subgraph "Testing"
        CATCH2["Catch2::Catch2WithMain"]
        TESTS["tests"]
    end
    
    CELL_SRC --> CELL
    CUAEV_SRC --> CUAEV
    TORCHANI_SRC --> TORCHANI
    
    TORCH --> CELL
    PYTHON --> CELL
    TORCH --> CUAEV
    PYTHON --> CUAEV
    TORCH --> TORCHANI
    CUAEV --> TORCHANI
    CELL --> TORCHANI
    
    CATCH2 --> TESTS
    TORCHANI --> TESTS
```

### Compilation Specifications

**cell_list Library**: Built from TorchANI sandbox submodule sources with C++17 standard and PyTorch/Python linking.

**cuaev Library**: CUDA-enabled library with specific optimizations:
- `TORCHANI_OPT` preprocessor definition enables CUDA intrinsics
- `-use_fast_math` NVCC flag for fast math library
- Custom CUB namespace definitions to avoid conflicts with PyTorch

**torchani Library**: Main interface library with comprehensive warning flags and special linking requirements:
- Force-loading of `cuaev` and `cell_list` using `LINKER:-force_load`
- `--no-as-needed` linker flag to ensure proper dependency resolution

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:234-287](), [CMakeLists.txt:289-323]()

### JIT Model Compilation

The build system includes a JIT compilation step for ANI models when `JIT_COMPILE_MODELS` is enabled:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["TorchScriptUtils_jit_compile_models"] --> B["Python Model Sources"]
    B --> C["JIT Compilation Process"]
    C --> D[".pt Model Files"]
    
    E["JIT_FORCE_RECOMPILATION"] -.-> C
    F["JIT_DISABLE_OPTIMIZATIONS"] -.-> C
    
    D --> G["Runtime Model Loading"]
```

This process converts Python-defined ANI models into TorchScript format for efficient C++ runtime loading.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:215-223]()

## Installation and Packaging

### RPATH Configuration

The build system implements sophisticated RPATH handling to ensure runtime library resolution:

```mermaid
graph TD
    A["SET_TORCHANI_LIBRARIES_INSTALL_RPATH"] --> B["Configure Install RPATH"]
    B --> C["${LIBTORCH_LIBRARY_DIR}"]
    B --> D["${CUDA_TOOLKIT_ROOT_DIR}"]
    B --> E["${CMAKE_INSTALL_FULL_LIBDIR}/Torchani"]
    
    C --> F["Runtime Library Resolution"]
    D --> F
    E --> F
    
    G["INSTALL_RPATH_USE_LINK_PATH"] --> F
```

The RPATH configuration prevents re-linking issues during installation and ensures libraries can locate dependencies regardless of system-wide CUDA installations.

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:340-364]()

### CMake Package Configuration

The build system generates complete CMake package configuration for downstream usage:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `TorchaniConfig.cmake` | Main configuration file with paths and targets |
| `TorchaniConfigVersion.cmake` | Version compatibility checking |
| `TorchaniTargets.cmake` | Exported target definitions |

**Installation Structure**:
- Libraries: `${CMAKE_INSTALL_LIBDIR}/Torchani/`
- Headers: `${CMAKE_INSTALL_INCLUDEDIR}/Torchani/`
- CMake files: `${CMAKE_INSTALL_DATAROOTDIR}/cmake/Torchani/`
- Fortran interface: `${CMAKE_INSTALL_DATAROOTDIR}/Torchani/Fortran/`

Sources: [CMakeLists.txt:393-461](), [cmake/TorchaniConfig.cmake.in:1-13]()

### Compiler and Version Validation

The build system includes strict compiler validation:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["Compiler Detection"] --> B{"GNU Compilers?"}
    B -->|No| C["FATAL_ERROR"]
    B -->|Yes| D["Version Check"]
    D --> E{"11.0 <= Version <= 13.2?"}
    E -->|No| F["FATAL_ERROR"]
```

This validation ensures compatibility with CUDA toolkit requirements and PyTorch ABI constraints.
